lyra.a: Lyra is a feminine given name of Greek and Latin origin meaning lyre. It is usually given in reference to the constellation and the Greek myth that inspired its naming. The name has associations with music and harmony and the night sky.

mabel.a: Mabel is an English female name derived from the Latin amabilis, "lovable, dear".

mack.a: Mack is a given name and nickname. Notable people with the name include:

macsen.e: Latin Maximus, specifically from 4th-century Roman co-emperor Magnus Maximus (in Welsh known as Macsen Wledig).

macy.e: Norman baronial surname from places named Massy in France, derived from a Gallo-Roman personal name Maccius.
macy.a: Macy is a female given name based on the surname Macy, which is itself derived from a French place name meaning "Maccius' estate". Other spelling variations of the name include Macie, Macey, and Maci. The name's popularity increased after Rowland Macy founded the Macy's chain of department stores.

maddie.a: Maddy or Maddie is a shortened form of the feminine given names Madeleine, Madeline, Madelyn, Madison, etc.

maddison.e: From Madde (a medieval diminutive of Maud and Magdalene) son.
maddison.a: Maddison is both a surname and a feminine given name. It is a variant spelling of Madison.

maddox.a: Maddox is a mainly male name in use in English speaking countries derived from a Welsh surname meaning "son of Madoc". The name Madoc means "fortunate" and is derived from the Welsh word mad.

madeline.e: Anglicized from French Madeleine, from Ancient Greek Μαγδαληνή or from Old High German Madalinde.

madelyn.a: Madelyn or Madalyn is a feminine first name, a variant of Madeline or Madeleine. Notable people with these names include:

madison.e: Usually derived from Mathieson (Matthew + -son), occasionally from Middle English Maddy (“Maud”) + -son. In the movie Splash, its use as a given name derives from Manhattan’s Madison Avenue.
madison.a: Madison is a surname of English origin that has become a popular given name in the United States, and to a lesser extent in Canada. Madison, also spelled Maddison, is a variant of Mathieson, meaning son of Matthew. It may also have come from son of Maddy, Maddy being a diminutive of Maud.

mae.a: Mae is a feminine given name primarily used in English-speaking countries. Often regarded as a variant of May, it is associated with the Roman goddess Maia, symbolizing spring, growth, and fertility.

maebh.a: Maeve, Meave, Maev or Maiv, Maiev ( mayv) is a female given name of Irish origin. It comes from the Irish name Méabh, which was spelt Meadhbh or Maedhbh in Early Modern Irish , Meḋḃ or Meaḋḃ in Middle Irish, and Medb in Old Irish .

maeva.a: Maeva or Maëva is a feminine given name.

maeve.e: Anglicized form of the Irish Méabh, from Middle Irish Medb and Meadhbh in Medieval irish. The name of a legendary queen of Connacht in the Ulster Cycle of Irish mythology.
maeve.a: Maeve, Meave, Maev or Maiv, Maiev ( mayv) is a female given name of Irish origin. It comes from the Irish name Méabh, which was spelt Meadhbh or Maedhbh in Early Modern Irish , Meḋḃ or Meaḋḃ in Middle Irish, and Medb in Old Irish .

maggie.a: Maggie or Maggy is a feminine given name. It can be a short form of Magdalena, Magnolia, Margaret, or Marigold.

magnus.e: Latin magnus (“great”), taken from the title of Carolus Magnus "Charlemagne" by an eleventh century king of Norway, and brought to Scotland in medieval times.
magnus.a: Magnus is a male given name. Notable people with the name include: Magnus (Roman usurper) (died 235) Magnus (consul 460) Magnus Forteman, 8th–9th century Frisian leader Magnus (bishop), Roman Catholic Bishop of Turku between 1291 and 1308 Magnus, Prince of Anhalt-Köthen Magnus W.

maha.a: Maha is an Arabic female given name meaning "half moon" or "beautiful eyes". The wild deer — or the Arabian oryx antelope, which is identified with the word mahā in some sources — has been traditionally celebrated in Arabic poetry for the beauty of its eyes.

mahir.a: Mahir is an Arabic given name meaning "skilled" or "expert". Notable people with the name include:

maia.a: Maia is a feminine given name. It may be in reference to the mythic mother of Hermes.

maira.e: First recorded as a given name of Latvians in 1935. From Marija (“Mary”).

maire.e: From Latin Maria, from Ancient Greek Μαρία, Μαριάμ, from Hebrew מִרְיָם. Cognate with Scottish Gaelic Màiri.
maire.a: Máire is a feminine given name. It is the Irish language form of Maria, which was in turn a Latin form of the Greek names Μαριαμ (Mariam), and Μαρια (Maria), found in the New Testament. Both New Testament names were forms of the Hebrew name מִרְיָם (Miryam).

mairead.a: Mairead, also spelt Maighread, is a feminine given name, the Scottish Gaelic equivalent of Margaret. The Irish form is spelt Mairéad, Máiréad, Maighréad, or Máighréad.

mairtin.e: From Latin Martinus, re-formed to contain the suffix -ín.
mairtin.a: Máirtín is an Irish given name.

maisie.e: From May (a pet form of Margaret) + -sie.
maisie.a: Maisie, also spelt Maisy or other minor variations, is a feminine given name of Scottish origin, derived from Mey (a pet form either of Mary or Margaret) and the diminutive suffix -sie.

maisy.a: Maisie, also spelt Maisy or other minor variations, is a feminine given name of Scottish origin, derived from Mey (a pet form either of Mary or Margaret) and the diminutive suffix -sie.

maitiu.a: Maitiú is the Irish form of Matthew, a masculine given name of biblical origin.

maja.a: Maja is a Slavic and German feminine given name.

maksymilian.a: Maksymilian is the Polish form of the male given name Maximilian.

malachi.e: From Latin Mālāchiās, from Ancient Greek Μαλαχίας, from Hebrew מַלְאָכִי, singular form of מַלְאָךְ (“angel; messenger; ambassadors”) with first-person singular personal pronoun as possessor.
malachi.a: Malachi is a male given name of Hebrew origin מַלְאָכִי‎ meaning "my messenger". The name is popularized by the Jewish prophet Malachi in the Bible.

malachy.e: From Irish Maolmhaodhóg and Maolseachnaill/Maolseachlainn, influenced by the etymologically unrelated name Malachi, which is of Hebrew origin.
malachy.a: Malachy is a given name of Irish origin. Notable people with the name include:

malaika.a: Malaika is a female given name.

malak.a: Malak is a given name. It derives from the Semitic word for "angel". . The plural of malak ("angels") is ملائكه malaa`ikahם malakim in Hebrew, and መላዕክት mala`ikt in Ge'ez.

malakai.e: Borrowed from Malakai and Malakai, equivalent to English Malachi.

malcolm.e: Royal name in Scotland, anglicised from various historical names equivalent to Scottish Gaelic Maol Chaluim or Calum, Irish Maol Colm, Middle Irish Máel Coluim, Old Irish Máel Columb
malcolm.a: Malcolm, Malcom, Máel Coluim, or Maol Choluim is a Scottish Gaelic given name meaning "devotee of Saint Columba". Maol "shavenhead" is Scottish Gaelic for monk.

mali.e: From French Mali, from or mali (“hippopotamus”).

malia.e: Borrowed from Malia (“Mary”) and in some cases from Mālia (“calm”).

maliha.a: Maliha is a feminine given name. The name definitely stems from the Arabic adjective singular "malāḥah مَلَاحَة" which the plural variant form is "malīḥ مَليح" or "milāḥ مِلَاح", meaning "state of being gorgeous or graceful" or "state of beauty, grace, elegance".

malik.a: Malik, Maleek, Maliq, Malique, Malick, Mallick, Mallik, or Malyk () is a given name of West Asian Semitic origin.

mara.a: Mara can be either a surname or a (usually female) first name. Mara is Irish for ocean.

marcel.e: Borrowed from French Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, diminutive of Marcus.
marcel.a: Marcel is an Occitan form of the Ancient Roman origin male given name Marcellus, which in Latin means "Belonging to Mars". The feminine counterpart of the name is Marcelle.

marco.e: From Marco Marco (Italian Marco, Portuguese Marco, Spanish Marco).
marco.a: Marco is an Italian masculine given name of Etruscan and Latin origin, derived from Marcus. It derives from the Roman god Mars.

marcus.e: Borrowing of Latin Marcus. Doublet of Mark.
marcus.a: Marcus is a masculine given name of Ancient Roman pre-Christian origin derived either from Etruscan Marce of unknown meaning or referring to the god Mars. Mars was identified as the Roman god of war.

margaret.e: From the name of 3rd century Saint Margaret the Virgin, from Middle English Margaret, from Old French Margaret (French Marguerite), from Latin Margarita, from Ancient Greek μαργαρίτης (“pearl”), ultimately from an Indo-Iranian source.
margaret.a: Margaret is a feminine given name, which means "pearl". It is of Latin origin, via Ancient Greek and ultimately from Old Iranian. It has been an English name since the 11th century, and remained popular throughout the Middle Ages.

margaux.a: Margaux is a French feminine given name.

margo.a: Margo or Margó is a female given name, a form of Margaret. In Estonia, it is mainly a male given name. Notable people or characters named Margo include:

margot.a: Margot is a feminine given name, a French diminutive of Marguerite that has long been used as an independent name. Variant spellings in use include Margo and Margaux. It is also occasionally a surname.

maria.a: Maria is a feminine given name. It is given in many languages influenced by Christianity.

marina.e: Name of an early virgin martyr venerated in the Orthodox Church, Latin Marīna, probably a feminine form of Marīnus, from marīnus (“of the sea”), or a variant of Marīa.
marina.a: Marina is a feminine given name. It is the female version of the Roman family name Marinus, which is a form of the Latin name Marius. The meaning of Marius might be connected to Mars, the Roman god of war, or with the Latin word maris, meaning virile.

mark.e: From Middle English Mark, from the praenomen (i.e. first name) Mārcus, derived from Mārs, the Roman god of war, originally Māvors, from *Māwortis.
mark.a: Mark is a common male name and is related to the Latin word Mars. It means "consecrated to the god Mars", and also may mean "God of war" or "to be warlike". Marcus was one of the three most common Roman given names.

marla.a: Marla is a female given name in English. It is a variant of the name Marlene, which comes from Mary Magdalene, the biblical woman to whom Jesus Christ first appeared after his resurrection.

marley.e: From several different places in England, from Old English mære (“boundary”) or myrig (“pleasant”) or mearþ (“marten”) + lēah (“woodland clearing”). In the first case, equivalent to mere#Etymology_2 + -leigh.

marlowe.a: Marlowe is both a surname and a given name. Notable people with the name include:

marnie.e: Possibly a contraction of Marina or a diminutive of Marian.
marnie.a: Marnie is a feminine given name sometimes said to be derived from the name Marina. Marna is a Swedish variant of Marina and also used as a Danish and Norwegian variant of Maren, which is derived from Maria or Marina.

marta.a: Marta is a female given name derived from the Aramaic name ܡܳܪܬܳܐ , which translates as "the lady" in English. It had the male form "Martinus" in Roman culture. It has been described as a cognate of Martha.

martha.a: Martha is a feminine given name . Patti, Patsy, and Patty were in use in Colonial America as English rhyming diminutives of the diminutive Mattie. Molly has been used as a diminutive of Martha since the 18th century.

martin.e: From Middle English Martin, from Latin Mārtīnus (“of or like Mars” or “little Mars”), Mars + -īnus. See Mārs for further etymology.
martin.a: Martin may either be a given name or surname. In Scotland, Martin or McMartin is a common surname of Scottish Gaelic origin. Martin is, however, more common as a masculine given name in many languages and cultures.

martina.e: Usually interpreted as the feminine form of the saints' name Martin, though there was an identical Roman name, likewise derived from Latin Martinus.
martina.a: Martina is a female given name, the female form of Martin and Martino.

marwa.a: Marwa or Marwah is an Arabic female given name derived from the word marū/maruw with the meaning of either minerals, 'flint(-stone)', 'quartz' or 'a hard stone of nearly pure silica'. However, the Arabic name for quartz is ṣawwān . The name is written Marva in the Persian form.

mary.a: Mary (, MAIR-ee) is a feminine given name, the English form of the name Maria, which was in turn a Latin form of the Greek name Μαρία, María or Μαριάμ, Mariam, found in the Septuagint and New Testament.

maryam.e: Borrowed from Arabic مَرْيَم and Persian مریم.

mason.a: Mason is a traditionally masculine given name, although recently the name has been used for either sex. Its origin is from the occupational surname Mason, which means "one who works with stone". It is also occasionally a nickname.

matei.a: Matei is a Romanian masculine given name and surname. It is derived from the given name Matthias and a is cognate to the English name Matthew.

mateo.e: From Spanish Mateo, from Latin Matthaeus, from Ancient Greek Ματθαῖος, from Hebrew מַתִּתְיָהוּ.
mateo.a: Mateo is a masculine given name, a form of Matthew used in Spanish and Croatian, similar to the Italian form Matteo.

mathias.a: Mathias, a given name and a surname which is a variant of Matthew (name), may refer to:

matias.e: Ultimately from Latin Matthias, from Ματθίας, from Biblical Hebrew מַתִּתְיָהוּ.

matilda.e: From Middle English Matilda, from Old French Mathilde, from Old High German Mahthilt, Mehthilt, from Proto-West Germanic *Mahtihild, from Proto-Germanic *Mahtihildiz; compare German Mechthild, Old English Mæþhild (“Matilda”).
matilda.a: Matilda, also spelled Mathilda and Martilda, is the English and Latin form of the Germanic female name Mahthildis, which derives from the Old High German "maht" (meaning "might and strength") and "hild" (meaning "battle").

matteo.e: From Latin Matthaeus, from Ancient Greek Ματθαῖος, from Hebrew מַתִּתְיָהוּ.
matteo.a: Matteo is the Italian form of the given name Matthew. Another form is Mattia. The Hebrew meaning of Matteo is "gift of god".

matthew.e: From earlier Matheu, from Old French Mathieu, from Latin Matthaeus, from Ancient Greek Ματθαῖος, from מַתַּי. Compare Hebrew מַתִּתְיָהוּ.
matthew.a: Matthew is an English language masculine given name. It ultimately derives from the Hebrew name "מַתִּתְיָהוּ" (Matityahu).

maura.e: Either from Irish Máire and Scottish Gaelic Màiri, or from Italian Maura. When borrowed from Irish, a.
maura.a: Maura is a female given name primarily used in English, Spanish, Italian, Greek, Scots Gaelic, and Irish. In Romance languages it appears as the feminine form of the Roman given name Maurus. In Gaelic languages it may be an Anglicisation of Máire, the Irish form of Mary.

maureen.e: Anglicized from Irish Máirín, diminutive of Máire, an Irish equivalent of Mary.
maureen.a: Maureen is a female name. In Gaelic, it is Máirín, a pet form of Máire , which is derived from the Hebrew Miriam. Some notable bearers of the name are:

maverick.e: The surname is most famously associated with Samuel Maverick, a rancher from Texas who did not brand his cattle. The surname is of uncertain origin, but known to date as far back as the 1500s in Devon, England.
maverick.a: Maverick is both a surname and a given name that is a transferred use of the British surname.

mavis.e: Coined at the end of the 19th century from mavis, a poetical name for the song thrush.
mavis.a: Mavis is a feminine given name, derived from a name for the common Old World song thrush.

max.e: German Max, diminutive of Maximilian in the 19th century, later also used as a nickname for Maxwell.
max.a: Max () is a unisex given name. For males, often short for Maximilian, Maxim, Maksym, Maxwell, Maxfield, or Maximus in English; Maximos in Greek; or Maxime or Maxence in French. For females, it is often short for Maxine.

maxim.a: Maxim (more accurately spelled Maksim assuming that "X" is not a consonant, but the conjunction of "K" and "S" sounds; "Maksym", or "Maxym") is an epicene (or gender-neutral) first name of Roman origin mainly given to males.

maximilian.e: From German Maximilian, ultimately of origin.
maximilian.a: Maximilian or Maximillian (Maximiliaan in Dutch and Maximilien in French) is a male name. The name "Max" is considered a shortening of "Maximilian" as well as of several other names, including but not limited to Maxwell.

maxwell.e: From an earlier form Mackeswell, meaning "Mack's well or spring", from Old English welle (“well”).
maxwell.a: Maxwell is a masculine given name. It is of English and Scottish origin, meaning "From Mack's Spring". The name originates as a place name from a location on the River Tweed in Scotland and first recorded in 1144 CE, spelled Mackeswell.

may.e: From Middle English May, Mai, from Old French mai, from Latin Maius (“Maia's month”), from Maia, a Roman earth goddess.
may.a: May is an English feminine given name. It is derived from the name of the month, which comes from Maia, the name of a Roman fertility goddess. It can also be a variant of the Arabic name Mai مي, which either means water or little gazelle.

maya.e: Spanish maya, from mayab (“flat”) or maaya, a self-designation of the northern Maya for themselves, in the form maya’ found in compounds and phrases e.g. maya’ wíinik (“Maya man”).
maya.a: Maya is a feminine name in various languages with various meanings. In the ancient Indian language Sanskrit, Māyā means "the illusory nature of reality or the illusion of creation", and is an alternate name of the Hindu goddess Lakshmi.

meabh.e: From Middle Irish Medb, from Proto-Celtic *medwā, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu. Compare Middle Irish medb (“intoxicating”), from Proto-Celtic *medwos.

medb.e: From Proto-Celtic *medwā, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰu. Compare Middle Irish medb (“intoxicating”), from Proto-Celtic *medwos.

megan.e: Welsh Megan, cognate with English Margaret, ultimately from an Indo-Iranian source.
megan.a: Megan is a Welsh feminine given name, originally a diminutive form of Margaret. Margaret is from the Greek μαργαρίτης (margarítēs), Latin margarīta, "pearl". Megan is one of the most popular Welsh-language names for women in Wales and England, and is commonly truncated to Meg.

melanie.e: From French Mélanie, from Latin Melania, the name of two Roman fifth century saints, from Ancient Greek μέλας (“black, dark”).
melanie.a: Melanie is a feminine given name derived from the Greek μελανία (melania), "blackness", and that from μέλας (melas), meaning "dark".

melina.a: Melina is a feminine given name of Greek origin, derived from the word "méli", which means "honey".

melisa.a: Melisa is a common feminine Turkish given name.

melissa.e: From Ancient Greek μέλισσα (“bee, honey, or honeybee”). In Ireland it is sometimes used as a feminine form of the Gaelic male name Maol Íosa.
melissa.a: Melissa is a feminine given name. The name comes from the Greek word μέλισσα (mélissa), "bee", which in turn comes from μέλι (meli), "honey". In Hittite, melit signifies "honey".

melody.e: From the noun melody; in regular use since the 20th century.
melody.a: Melody is a modern English feminine given name taken from the vocabulary word melody, which is ultimately derived from the Greek μελῳδία, melōidía, "singing, chanting").

meredith.a: Meredith is a Welsh given name, and a surname common in parts of Wales. As a personal name, it was historically usually given to boys, but it has more recently been given mainly to girls, especially outside Wales. Meredith has many derivatives that have also become personal names and surnames.

mia.a: Mia is a feminine given name in popular use worldwide. It originated as a diminutive of Maria and other names such as Amelia and Emilia, and was rarely used as an independent given name prior to the 20th century.

micah.e: From Hebrew מִיכָה, shortened form of מִיכַיְהוּ (“who is like Yahweh”).
micah.a: Micah is a given name. Micah is the name of several people in the Tanakh, and means "Who is like God?”. The name is sometimes found with theophoric extensions.

michael.e: From Middle English Michael, from Old French Michel, Old English Michahel, from their source Latin Michaēl,Michāhēl, from Ancient Greek Μῐχᾱήλ, from Biblical Hebrew מִיכָאֵל.
michael.a: Michael is a common masculine given name usually thought to be from the Hebrew rhetorical question מי כאל , "Who [is] like [the Hebrew god] El?", thus being a theophoric name whose answer is "there is none like El", or "there is none as famous and powerful as God." This question is known in Latin…

michaela.e: From Michael + a. Latinate feminine form of Michael, first appearing as an anglicisation of the Portuguese ("Micaela") and Spanish ("Micaela").
michaela.a: Michaela is a female given name. It is a female form of the Hebrew name Michael , which means "Who is like God". As of 2008, it was 357th in rank for newborn girls in the United States, and 325th in England and Wales.

micheal.e: From Latin Michael, Michahel, from Biblical Hebrew מִיכָאֵל (“who is like God?”).
micheal.a: Micheal is a masculine given name. It is sometimes an anglicized form of the Irish name Mícheál (also rendered Micheál and Michéal); or the Scottish Gaelic name Mìcheal.

michelle.e: French Michelle, feminine form of French Michel (“Michael”), Hebrew מִיכָאֵל (“who is like God?”).
michelle.a: Michelle is a given name, originally a variant of Michèle, the French feminine form of Michel, derived from the Hebrew name Michael meaning "Who is like God?". The usual Latin feminine form of the name was Michaela, with Michael the vernacular form for both men and women.

mikael.a: Mikael is a masculine given name, a variant of the Hebrew name Michael , which means "Who is like God". It is used predominantly throughout Scandinavia and Finland. Mikaela is the feminine form of the name.

mikail.a: Michael is a common masculine given name usually thought to be from the Hebrew rhetorical question מי כאל , "Who [is] like [the Hebrew god] El?", thus being a theophoric name whose answer is "there is none like El", or "there is none as famous and powerful as God." This question is known in Latin…

mikayla.a: Michaela is a female given name. It is a female form of the Hebrew name Michael , which means "Who is like God". As of 2008, it was 357th in rank for newborn girls in the United States, and 325th in England and Wales.

mikey.a: Mikey is a masculine given name, often a diminutive form (hypocorism) of Michael or Mitchell. It may also refer to:

mikolaj.a: Mikołaj is the Polish cognate of given name Nicholas, used both as a given name and a surname.

mila.e: From a diminutive in many languages, etc.) of female given names containing the element Mil-, -mila ("grace, beloved"), such as Ludmila, Milena, Milica, and of the cognates of Emily. Also from Spanish Mila.
mila.a: Mila is a feminine Slavic name originating from Central or Eastern Europe. It is a diminutive of Slavic names beginning or ending with Mila which derived from the element Mil meaning "gracious" or "dear". It is also used among the Spanish as a short-hand for Milagros, meaning "miracles".

milan.e: Middle English Milane, Melan, etc., from Old English Mæġelan, Megelan, Mediolana burg, etc. under influence from early forms of French Milan, from Mediolāna etc., from Latin Mediolānum, q.v.
milan.a: Milan is a common Slavic male name and less commonly, a Roman name. It is derived from the Slavic element mil, with meanings kind, loving, and gracious. Milan was originally a diminutive or nickname for those whose Slavic names began with "Mil-".

milana.a: Milan is a common Slavic male name and less commonly, a Roman name. It is derived from the Slavic element mil, with meanings kind, loving, and gracious. Milan was originally a diminutive or nickname for those whose Slavic names began with "Mil-".

milena.a: Milena is a Slavic feminine given name. It is derived from the Proto-Slavic mil, meaning 'kind', 'dear'. It is the feminine form of the masculine names Milan and Milen.

miles.e: From given name Milo, of problematic origin, possibly from an unknown element, or a short form of names beginning with mil- "grace, favor". The English form is associated by folk etymology with Latin mīles (“soldier”).
miles.a: Miles or Myles () is a Norman French masculine given name. It might have been a changed diminutive of the name Michael that was influenced by miles, the Latin word for a soldier, because of associations with Archangel Michael, the Roman Catholic patron saint of the military.

miley.e: Popularised as a female name by American pop singer Miley Ray Cyrus (nicknamed Miley from "smiley").
miley.a: Miley is a unisex English given name. It first entered the top 1,000 names used for newborn girls in the United States in 2007 and has continued to be well used. Spelling variants of the name in use include, among others, Milee, Mileigh, Mylee, Myleigh, and Mylie.

miller.e: English surname, capitalization of miller. Also compare Milner, Millward, Müller, Mueller, Mulder, Molenaar, Meunier, Molinaro, Molinero, Molnár, Mlinar, Młynarczyk.

millicent.e: From the Old French Melisende, from Old High German Amalasuntha, Amalaswintha, from the roots *amalą (“hard work”) + *swinþaz (“strong”).
millicent.a: Millicent or Milicent is a feminine given name that has been in use since the Middle Ages. The English form Millicent derives from the Old French Melisende, stemming from the Germanic name Amalasuintha (from amal meaning 'work' and swinth meaning 'strength').

millie.a: Millie is a feminine given name. It is often short for Emily, Millicent, Mildred, Camille, Camilla, Camila, Emilia, Maximillian, Malishka, or Amelia.

milly.a: Millicent or Milicent is a feminine given name that has been in use since the Middle Ages. The English form Millicent derives from the Old French Melisende, stemming from the Germanic name Amalasuintha (from amal meaning 'work' and swinth meaning 'strength').

milo.a: Milo is a masculine given name and a surname with multiple origins. The name was used in medieval England as the Latin version of Miles or Mile meaning soldier. It is also an ancient Greek name derived from milos, meaning "yew tree".

mina.a: Mina is a given name with a variety of origins.

minnie.a: Minnie is a feminine given name. It can be a diminutive (hypocorism) of Minerva, Winifred, Wilhelmina, Willemina, Winona, Margaret, Hermione, Jasmine, Mary, Miriam, Maria, Marie, Naomi, Miranda, Clementine, Dominique, Dominic, or Amelia. It may refer to:

mira.e: Named by the astronomer Johannes Hevelius in 1662, from Latin mīrus (“wonderful, surprising”).
mira.a: Mira is a feminine given name with varying meanings. In the Romance languages, it is related to the Latin word ''mirus'' for 'wonder' and 'wonderful'.

miran.a: Miran is a given name and surname. The name Miran is derived from the word Mir (eng. peace) and the suffix 'an' which is a very common component of Slavic names. (Keber, Janez, Leksikon imen (COBISS))

miriam.e: From Hebrew מִרְיָם, possibly from מרים (“bitter”), from a root מר (m-r) meaning "to be bitter". The meaning of this name which is the Old Testament equivalent of Mary has been debated for centuries.
miriam.a: Miriam is a feminine given name recorded in Biblical Hebrew in the Book of Exodus as the name of the sister of Moses, the prophetess Miriam. Spelling variants include French Myriam, German Mirjam, Mirijam; hypocoristic forms include Mira, Miri and Mimi (commonly given in Israel).

mohamad.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

mohamed.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

mohammad.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

mohammed.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

mollie.a: Molly (also spelled Molli or Mollie) is a diminutive of the feminine name Mary that, like other English hypocorisms in use since the Middle Ages, substituted l for r. Molly evolved from the English diminutive Mally. English surnames such as Moll, Mollett, and Mollison are derived from Molly.

molly.e: From Moll, diminutive lambdacism of Mary y.
molly.a: Molly (also spelled Molli or Mollie) is a diminutive of the feminine name Mary that, like other English hypocorisms in use since the Middle Ages, substituted l for r. Molly evolved from the English diminutive Mally. English surnames such as Moll, Mollett, and Mollison are derived from Molly.

monroe.e: From Old English mann (“human being, person, man”) + Roe, a river in Northern Ireland, meaning "man from the River Roe".
monroe.a: Monroe is a unisex given name, a transferred use of the surname.

montgomery.e: From a surname, from a place in Normandy (for "Gomeric's hill"). Gumaric was a personal name composed of *gumô (“man”) and *rīks (“ruler”) (whence the modern French surnames Gomery, Gommery and Gumery or the Galician placename Gomariz).

monty.a: Monty is a masculine given name, often a short form of Montgomery, Montague and other similar names. It is also a surname. Notable people with the name or nickname include:

morgan.a: Morgan is a name of Welsh and Breton origin. Traditionally, it is a masculine name in Wales and Brittany, but has been become unisex in modern times. Morgan is also used as a surname, derived from the given name.

moses.e: From Latin Mōsēs, from Ancient Greek Μωσῆς, from earlier Μωυσῆς, from Biblical Hebrew מֹשֶׁה. Further etymology is unclear, but it is sometimes conjectured to derive from msj (“to give birth to”), a common element in Egyptian names of the…
moses.a: Moses , Moises, Moyses , Moishe , Moshe , Musa , or Movses is a male given name, after the biblical figure Moses.

moshe.a: Moshe is the Hebrew version of the masculine given name Moses, including of the Biblical figure Moses.

moya.a: Moya is a feminine given name.

moyra.a: Moyra is a female given name.

muhammad.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

muhammed.a: Muhammad is an Arabic given male name meaning "praiseworthy". The name comes from the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada , meaning "to praise", which itself comes from the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

muireann.a: Muireann is an Irish-language feminine given name.

muiris.e: From Mauritius, derived from Maurus (“Moor; dark, swarthy”).

murphy.e: From Irish Ó Murchadha (“descendant of Murrough”), Mac Murchaidh (“Son of Murrough”), etc. See Muircath.
murphy.a: Murphy is a given name of Irish origin. Notable people and characters with the name include:

murray.e: Scottish surname derived from the place name Moray in northeastern Scotland, from Moravia, Morauia, from Scottish Gaelic Moireibh, Moireabh, Moreb, ultimately from Proto-Celtic *mori (“sea”) + *trebā (“settlement”).
murray.a: Murray is an English masculine given name, originally derived from the Scottish and Irish surname Murray. Notable people with the name include:

musa.a: Musa is an Arabic male name and cognate for "Moses".

mustafa.a: Mustafa is one of the names of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. It is Arabic for "chosen, selected, appointed, preferred". It is a common male given name and derived surname in Muslim-majority countries.

mya.e: A modern phonetic spelling of Maia or Maya.
mya.a: Mya is a primarily feminine given name of uncertain origins. One source considers it to be a 20th-century phonetic spelling of the name Maya or Mia, names that have multiple, different meanings and origins in different languages.

myah.e: Rare fanciful spelling of Mya, Maia, Maya.

myles.a: Myles is a masculine given name, a variant spelling of Miles.

myra.e: First used by the poet Fulke Greville, possibly as an anagram of Mary.

nadia.e: Originally the French spelling of На́дя, an informal Russian pet form of the virtue name Наде́жда (“Nadezhda, Nadyezhda”), from наде́жда (“hope”), entered as a translation of the Ancient Greek word from ἐλπίς (“hope”) with the same…
nadia.a: Nadia is a female name. Variations include Nadja, Nadya, Nadine, Nadiya, and Nadiia. Most variations of the name are derived from Arabic, Slavic languages, or both.

naila.a: Naila or Na'ila is a female given name of Arabic origin meaning "gracious".

nana.a: Nana is a given name that has different origins in several countries across the world. Its use as a feminine or masculine name varies culturally.

nancy.e: Medieval diminutive of Ann and Agnes. Compare Betsy, Patsy.
nancy.a: Nancy is a feminine English language given name. The name Nancy was originally a diminutive form of Annis, a medieval English vernacular form of Agnes, which means "pure" or "holy". In some English dialects, "mine" was used instead of "my" and "Mine Ancy" eventually became Nancy.

naomi.e: From Hebrew נָעֳמִי, from + ־ִי (“my, of me”).
naomi.a: Naomi or Noemi is a given name of separate biblical Hebrew and Japanese origin used in various languages and cultures.

natalia.e: Latin natale (“birthday (of the Lord)”), referring to birth on Christmas Day, name of an early martyr.
natalia.a: Natalia is a female given name with the original Late Latin meaning of "Christmas Day" (cf. Latin natale domini). In Russian, a common diminutive is Natasha .

natalie.e: From the form of the saint's name Natalia, from nātālis (diēs) (“birthday [of Christ], Christmas”).
natalie.a: Natalie is a feminine given name derived from the Latin phrase natale domini, meaning "birth of the Lord". Further alternative spellings of the name include Nathalie, Natalee, and Natalia/Natalija.

natan.a: Natan is a masculine given name, from which Nathan is derived, and a surname. It may refer to:

natasha.e: Borrowed from Russian Ната́ша, an informal pet form of Ната́лья, cognate to Natalie.

nate.a: Nate is a given name, frequently used as a diminutive of Nathan, Nathanael or Nathaniel.

nathan.e: From Hebrew נָתָן (“gave”). Also short for Jonathan.
nathan.a: Nathan is a masculine given name. It is derived from the Hebrew verb נָתָן meaning gave .

nathanael.e: From Ancient Greek Ναθαναήλ, from Biblical Hebrew נְתַנְאֵל.

nathaniel.e: Modification, under influence of Daniel, of Nathanael, from Ancient Greek Ναθαναήλ, from Biblical Hebrew נְתַנְאֵל.

neal.a: Neal (Neil) is a surname and masculine given name of the Gaelic origin. The name may be derived from words meaning "cloud", "passionate", "victory", "honour" or "champion".

neasa.a: Neasa is an Irish feminine given name.

neave.e: Two main origins: * A variant of the English surname Neve. * Variant of Nevay, a Scottish habitational surname.

ned.a: Ned is an English given name and variant of Ed, sometimes short for Edward, Edmund, Edgar, or Edwin.

neil.a: Neil is a masculine name of Irish origin. The name is an anglicisation of the Irish Niall which is of disputed derivation. The Irish name may be derived from words meaning "cloud", "passionate", "victory", "honour" or "champion".

nel.a: Nel is both a South African (Afrikaans) surname and a Dutch feminine given name. Notable people with the name include:

nela.a: Nela is a Croatian, Czech and Slovak feminine given name that serves as a diminutive form of Antonela and Antonie in Croatia, Czech Republic and Slovakia.

nella.e: Possibly borrowed as a diminutive from German Cornelia.
nella.a: Nella is a feminine given name which may refer to:

nellie.e: Suffixed with -ie, compare Noll and Neddie, respectively from Oliver and Edward.

neo.e: Recent coinage from the prefix neo- (“new”). Popularized by a character in the science-fiction film The Matrix (1999), where it is explained as an anagram of "(the) One".
neo.a: Neo is a given name of the following notable people: Chua Jim Neo , Singaporean chef and cookbook writer Gen Neo (born 1989), Singaporean singer-songwriter, producer and composer Neo Maema (born 1995), South African football midfielder Neo Makama (born 1981), Mosotho football striker Neo Masisi…

nessa.a: Nessa is a short version of Vanessa and a feminine given name.

nevaeh.e: From heaven, spelled backwards. Popular since 2000 when the rock singer Sonny Sandoval gave the name to his baby daughter.
nevaeh.a: Nevaeh is a feminine given name which was coined by spelling heaven backwards. It peaked in popularity in the 2000s and 2010s but remains one of the most popular girls' names as of 2020.

nevin.e: A rare Anglicization of Irish Naomhán, a diminutive of naomh (“saint”).

nia.a: Nia is a given name which appears in many cultures. In Bulgaria, it is a short form of the feminine name Evgenia.

niall.e: From Old Irish Níall, of uncertain original meaning. Suggestions include nél (“cloud”) and nïa (“champion”).
niall.a: Niall is a male given name of Irish origin. The original meaning of the name is unknown, but popular modern sources have suggested that it means "champion" .

niamh.e: From the noun niamh (“brightness, lustre, sheen”), from Middle Irish níam (“brilliance, beauty”), itself from Old Irish ném (“lustre”).
niamh.a: Niamh is an Irish feminine given name (meaning "bright" or "radiant"), anglicised as Neve, Nieve, Neave, Neavh or Neeve. In Irish mythology, Niamh is the daughter of the god of the sea, Manannán mac Lir and one of the queens of Tír na nÓg, the land of eternal youth.

nicholas.e: From Middle English Nicholas, from Old French Nicholas, from Latin Nīcolāus, from Ancient Greek Νικόλαος, from νίκη + λαός.
nicholas.a: Nicholas is a male name, the Anglophone version of an ancient Greek name in use since antiquity, and cognate with the modern Greek Νικόλαος, Nikolaos. It originally derived from a combination of two Greek words meaning 'victory' and 'people'.

nico.a: Nico is a unisex given name.

nicolas.a: Nicolas or Nicolás may refer to masculine given names cognate to English Nicholas. The given name Nicolas is widely used in Brazil and France . The variant Nicolás is widely used in Spanish-speaking countries.

nicole.e: French Nicole, the feminine form of Nicolas (“Nicholas”).
nicole.a: Nicole is a feminine given name and a surname.

nieve.a: Niamh is an Irish feminine given name (meaning "bright" or "radiant"), anglicised as Neve, Nieve, Neave, Neavh or Neeve. In Irish mythology, Niamh is the daughter of the god of the sea, Manannán mac Lir and one of the queens of Tír na nÓg, the land of eternal youth.

nikodem.a: Nikodem is a masculine given name. It is a variant of the given name Nicodemus.

nikolas.a: Nikolas is a given name and a surname. Notable people with the name include the following:

nila.e: From Sanskrit नील (“of a dark colour; blue; black”), নীলা (“blue”), or related words in other Indian subcontinent languages.

nina.e: Borrowed into English in the nineteenth century, apparently from several sources. Many borrowings are of Russian Ни́на, the name of a Georgian saint in the fourth century, also known as Nino, of obscure origin and meaning, possibly…
nina.a: Nina is a feminine given name with various origins and alternate spellings accordingly. Nina may also serve as a short form of names ending in "-nina/-ina", such as Clementina, Christina, or Giannina.

noa.a: Noa is both a male and female given and family name. In Israel, the name Noa , which means "movement" is primarily a popular given name for girls.

noah.a: Noah is historically an English male given name derived from the Biblical figure Noah in Hebrew. It is most likely of Hebrew in origin from the root word "nuach”/“nuakh”, meaning rest.

noel.e: From Middle English Nowel, borrowed from Old French Noel (“Christmas”), from Latin nātālis [diēs Dominī] (“birth[day of the Lord]”).
noel.a: Noel or Noël is a given name, often given to both girls and boys born over the Christmas period. Noel derives from the Old French "Noël", meaning "Christmas". It is a variant (and later replacement) of "nael", which itself comes from the Latin natalis, meaning "birth".

noelle.e: From French Noëlle, the feminine form of the male given name Noël.
noelle.a: Noelle or Noëlle is the feminine form of the unisex name Noel. It derives from the old French Noël, "Christmas," a variant (and later a replacement) of nael, which itself derives from the Latin natalis, "birthday".

nola.a: Nola is both a surname and a given name. Notable people with the name include:

nolan.e: Anglicized from Irish Ó Nualláin, diminutive of nuall (“chariot-fighter, champion”).
nolan.a: Nolan is a male given name of Irish origin meaning "champion".

nollaig.e: From Old Irish Notlaic, from Latin nātālīcia (“a birthday party”), from nātālis (“natal”), from nātus (“born”). Compare Welsh Nadolig, Breton Nedeleg and French Noël.
nollaig.a: Nollaig is an Irish language unisex given name. Originating from the Latin for Christmas, it is the equivalent to English Noel or Noelle.

noor.a: Noor is a common Arabic unisex given name meaning 'light', from the Arabic al-Nur . Feminine variants include Noora, Nora, Norah, Noura, and Nura. It is also used as a surname.

nora.e: Short form of Eleanor, rarely, of Honora.
nora.a: Nora or Norah is a feminine given name. It mainly originates as a short form of Honora (also Honoria), a common Anglo-Norman name, ultimately derived from the Latin word Honor (with that meaning). In Hungary, the name Nóra originates as a short form of Eleonóra.

noreen.a: Noreen is an Irish given name, anglicised from Nóirín. It is also an Arabic name with the forms Nourine, Noureen, and Noorin. Another spelling is Norene, Norine and Norinne.

noura.a: Noura is an Arabic-origin female given name and a surname, derived from the name Noor, meaning "light". People with the name include:

nova.a: Nova is a unisex given name of Latin origin meaning "new". It is in regular use for both males and females. In the United States, the name has been in use since the 1800s.

nuala.e: A shortened from of Fionnuala, from Old Irish Finnguala, from find (“fair”) + guala (“shoulder”).
nuala.a: Nuala is an Irish feminine given name, derived from Irish mythology - being either a diminutive form of Fionnuala ("fair shoulder"), the daughter of Lir, or an alternate name for Úna (perhaps meaning "lamb"), wife of Finvarra, king of the fairies.

nuh.e: Ultimately from Arabic نُوح, sometimes through other languages.
nuh.a: Nuh is a masculine given name. It is the Arabic form of Noah.

oakley.e: From Old English Āclēa, from āc (“oak”) + lēah (“woodland clearing, glade”), thus a clearing in an oak forest; equivalent to oak + -leigh. Compare Ackley, Akeley and Oakleigh, which have the same origin.
oakley.a: Oakley is a unisex given name of English origin that is a transferred use of an English place name and surname meaning “oak clearing”.

obie.e: Named after the actress Merle Oberon, whose husband Lucien Ballard used this kind of lighting to hide small scars on her face after a car accident.

ocean.e: From ocean (“sea”), inspired by the fashionable French female name Océane.

octavia.e: From Latin Octāvia, feminine form of the gens name Octāvius, from octavus (“the eighth”).
octavia.a: Octavia is a feminine given name of Latin origin meaning eight that derives from the Octavia gens.

odhran.e: From Old Irish Odrán, originally from odur + -án.
odhran.a: Odhrán is an Irish language masculine given name. It is usually anglicised as Odhran (without a fada), Oran or Orin. The feminine equivalent of the name is Odharnait.

odin.e: From Old Norse Óðinn, from Proto-Germanic *Wōdanaz. Related to od (“mad, wild, frenzied”). Cognate with Icelandic Óðinn, Óðin, Oden, English Woden, German Wotan, and Dutch Woen.
odin.a: Odin is both a surname and a given name.

odran.a: Odhrán is an Irish language masculine given name. It is usually anglicised as Odhran (without a fada), Oran or Orin. The feminine equivalent of the name is Odharnait.

oisin.e: From oisín (“fawn”), from os + -ín; name of a hero in Irish mythology.
oisin.a: Oisín is an Irish male given name; meaning "fawn" or "little deer", derived from the Irish word os ("deer") + -ín (diminutive suffix). It is sometimes anglicized as Osheen ( OSH-een) or spelt without the acute accent (fada), as Oisin.

olive.e: Medieval form of the saint's name Oliva "olive"; revived in the 19th century when flower and plant names became fashionable.
olive.a: Olive is a feminine given name of English origin meaning olive tree. The name is associated with peace because of the symbolism of the olive branch. An olive wreath has traditionally been worn by champions as a symbol of victory.

oliver.e: Middle English Oliver, from Old French Olivier, by folk etymology derived from the name Olīvārius, but probably representing an form of Old Norse Óleifr (“ancestral + relic”) (modern Danish Olaf and Swedish Olof), or Proto-Germanic *ala-…
oliver.a: Oliver is a masculine given name of Old French and Medieval British origin. The name has been generally associated with the Latin term olivarius, meaning "olive tree planter", or "olive branch bearer".

olivia.e: From Latin Olīva, an early saints’ name from olīva (“olive; olive branch”). First popularized by Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
olivia.a: Olivia is a feminine given name in the English language. It is derived from Latin oliva, olive. Both Oliva and Olivia were Latinate forms in use in English-speaking countries as early as the 13th century.

olivier.a: Olivier is a French and Dutch masculine given name form of Oliver which may refer to:

oliwier.a: Oliwier is a Polish masculine given name form of Oliver.

ollie.e: From, from Latin olivarius (“olive tree”) (from oliva (“olive”)), and.
ollie.a: Ollie is a given name and a nickname, often as a shortened form of Oliver, Olive, Olympia, Olga, or Olivia. Variants include Olie, Oli, Oly, and Olly.

omar.a: Omar or Umar is the most common Arabic rendition of a series of names, predominantly masculine given names, originating in the Arabic language.

omari.e: Borrowed from Arabic عمري. The surname is predominantly found in Tanzania.

oona.a: Oona is a feminine given name. It is an anglicisation of the Irish-language name Úna. Apart from in Ireland, it is also a popular name in Finland.

oonagh.e: Variant spelling of Oona, Una, Anglicized from Úna.
oonagh.a: Oona is a feminine given name. It is an anglicisation of the Irish-language name Úna. Apart from in Ireland, it is also a popular name in Finland.

opal.a: Opal is a primarily feminine given name derived from the name of the gemstone opal. The gemstone is the birthstone for October. Its name is derived from the Sanskrit upala , which means 'jewel'.

ophelia.e: Borrowed from Italian Ofelia, coined by the poet Jacopo Sannazaro in his poem Arcadia (1504), probably from the Ancient Greek ὠφέλειᾰ (“help, aid, succour”).
ophelia.a: Ophelia is a feminine given name, probably derived from the Ancient Greek word ὠφέλεια (ōphéleia, "benefit"). The name is best known as a character from William Shakespeare's Hamlet who has a tragic end.

oran.e: Ultimately Arabic وَهْرَان, from a term meaning "lion".
oran.a: Oran is a masculine given name and a surname. People with the name include:

orfhlaith.a: Órlaith is a feminine Irish given name. The meaning of the name derives from the Irish words ór "golden" and flaith "prince", though since names formed with "flaith" are almost exclusively feminine, it is usually interpreted as meaning "princess". The name is sometimes anglicised as Orla or Orlagh.

orhan.a: Orhan is a Turkish surname and masculine given name that means Khan of the fortress. Notable people with the name include:

orin.a: Or(r)in is an anglicised spelling of the Irish given name Odhrán, historically spelled Oḋrán.

orion.e: From Middle English Orioun, from Latin Ōrīōn, from Ancient Greek Ὠρίων, speculatively, though without any firm evidence.
orion.a: Orion is both a surname and a male given name usually derived from the character from Greek mythology or the constellation named for the character. The name has increased in usage in recent years along with other mythological names.

orla.e: Anglicized version of Irish Órfhlaith (“golden princess”), from ór (“gold”) + flaith (“princess”).
orla.a: Orla is an anglicisation of Órfhlaith, a feminine given name of Irish origin. The name is often interpreted as meaning "golden princess", as it is derived from the Irish words ór ("gold") and flaith (literally "prince"; its full feminine form being banfhlaith).

orlagh.a: Orla is an anglicisation of Órfhlaith, a feminine given name of Irish origin. The name is often interpreted as meaning "golden princess", as it is derived from the Irish words ór ("gold") and flaith (literally "prince"; its full feminine form being banfhlaith).

orlaith.a: Órlaith is a feminine Irish given name. The meaning of the name derives from the Irish words ór "golden" and flaith "prince", though since names formed with "flaith" are almost exclusively feminine, it is usually interpreted as meaning "princess". The name is sometimes anglicised as Orla or Orlagh.

orlando.e: From Italian Orlando (“Roland”), ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *Hrōþiland. The city in Florida has gone by the name since 1857, perhaps in honor of the soldier Orlando Reeves, whom the Seminoles killed there in 1835.
orlando.a: Orlando is a masculine given name, originally an Italian form of the given name Roland.

orson.a: Orson is a masculine given name derived from the Old French word for "bear cub" (ourson). Notable people and characters with the name Orson include:

oscar.e: From Middle Irish Oscar, probably from Old Irish oscar (“outsider, newcomer”), though traditionally analyzed as oss (“deer”) + carae (“friend”).
oscar.a: Oscar or Oskar is a masculine given name of English, Old Norse and Irish origin.

osian.a: Osian is a Welsh masculine given name, derived from the Irish legendary poet and warrior Oisín. The name is derived from the Irish for "little deer". Osian was the 22nd most popular name for baby boys in Wales in 2017.

oskar.a: Oscar or Oskar is a masculine given name of English, Old Norse and Irish origin.

osman.a: Osman refers to two different names: Osman or Usman is the Turkish, Kurdish, Persian, and Urdu transliteration of the Arabic masculine given name Uthman.

otis.e: A patronymic surname derived from genitive case of the given name Ote, Ode, cognate to modern Otto.
otis.a: Otis is a male given name derived from an English surname, which was in turn derived from Ode, a variant form of Odo and Otto. The name also has origins in the Ars Goetia, it is a variation of the name Botis. Otis is also a male nickname from Otieno, with its roots in the Luo tribe in Kenya.

ottilie.a: Ottilie is a feminine given name. It is a French derivative of the medieval German masculine name Otto and, like other related Germanic names beginning with the prefixes Ad-, Aut-, Od-, Ot-, Oth-, or Ud-, has the meaning "prosperous in battle", "riches", "prosperous" or "wealth".

otto.e: German Otto, short form of compound names (such as Otachar, Ottokar) beginning with Proto-West Germanic *aud, from Proto-Germanic *audaz (“wealth, riches”) (cognate of English Ed- in Edgar, Edmund, Edward, Edith, etc.).
otto.a: Otto is a masculine German given name and a surname. It originates as an Old High German short form (variants Audo, Odo, Udo) of Germanic names beginning in aud-, an element meaning "wealth, prosperity". The name is recorded from the 7th century (Odo, son of Uro, courtier of Sigebert III).

ovie.a: Ovie is a given name, nickname and surname.

ozzie.a: Ozzie or Ozzy is a masculine given name, sometimes a short form (hypocorism) of Oswald, Oscar, Osborne, Osman and Ozymandias and other names, surname and nickname which may refer to:

ozzy.a: Ozzie or Ozzy is a masculine given name, sometimes a short form (hypocorism) of Oswald, Oscar, Osborne, Osman and Ozymandias and other names, surname and nickname which may refer to:

paddy.a: Paddy is a unisex given name. It is often short for Patrick, Patricia, or Pádraig. Notable people include:

padraig.e: From Latin Patricius, likely via. Replaced Old Irish Cothraige, a much earlier borrowing as shown by the replacement of Latin p with c.

paige.e: Variant of Page, from page, from Old French page, possibly via paggio, from pagius (“servant”), probably from Ancient Greek παιδίον (“boy, lad”), from παῖς (“child”)
paige.a: Paige is an English surname and given name. The surname is a variant of Page, an occupational name derived from page. Its use as a given name was transferred from the surname.

paisley.a: Paisley is an English and Scottish surname and a given name derived from the surname.

paloma.a: Paloma is a Spanish female given name, derived from Latin "palumbus", which means "dove", a symbol of peace. The name also can be understood as the Holy Spirit symbolized in this bird.

paris.e: From Middle English Parys, Paris, from Old French Paris, from the name of an earlier settlement, Lutetia Parisiorum (“Lutetia of the Parisii”), from Latin Parīsiī, a tribe, from *parios (“cauldron”), from Proto-Celtic *kʷaryos, from…
paris.a: Paris is a unisex given name. It is of Greek origin and is common among Anglophone countries.

parker.a: Parker is an English-language unisex given name of Old English origin, meaning 'park keeper', hence also an Old English occupational surname. Parker was more common in the 19th century as a personal name than it is now. The name has variants.

patricia.e: From Latin patricia (“noble”); later also seen as the feminine form of the saint's name Patrick.
patricia.a: Patricia is a feminine given name of Latin origin. Derived from the Latin word patrician, meaning 'noble', it is the feminine form of the masculine given name Patrick. Another well-known variant is Patrice.

patrick.e: From Middle English Patrick, from Latin Patricius (“patrician”), the name of an early Irish saint.
patrick.a: Patrick is a male given name of Latin origin. It is derived from the Roman name Patricius (meaning patrician, i.e. 'father', 'nobleman').

paul.a: Paul is an English as well as Dutch, French and German masculine given name. The Roman and subsequently Christian derived name and its variations can also be a surname.

payton.e: Habitational surname from a minor place in Sussex, from the personal name Pǣga + tūn (“enclosure; settlement, town”).
payton.a: Payton is a given name in use in English speaking countries. One source indicates the name comes from a surname derived from a place name meaning "Pœga's town" in Old English. Another source indicates the name means "fighting man's estate".

peadar.e: From Old Irish Petur, from Latin Petrus, from Ancient Greek Πέτρος, from πέτρος (“stone, rock”).
peadar.a: Peadar is a masculine given name in Irish and Scottish Gaelic (in Manx the name is spelt Peddyr). The names are ultimately derived from the Greek word petros 'stone, rock', making them cognates to English Peter.

pearl.e: From pearl. * From 珠江 (“Pearl River”); 珠 (“pearl”). * From Wai Momi (“pearl water”); momi (“pearl”).
pearl.a: Pearl is a unisex given name derived from the English word pearl, a hard, roundish object produced within the soft tissue of a living, shelled mollusk. Pearls are commonly used in jewelry-making. The name has a history of usage among Jews.

pedro.a: Pedro is a masculine given name. Pedro is the Spanish, Portuguese, and Galician name for Peter. Its French equivalent is Pierre while its English and Germanic form is Peter.

peggy.a: Peggy is a female first name (often curtailed to "Peg") derived from Meggy, a diminutive version of the name Margaret.

penelope.e: From Ancient Greek Πηνελόπη, possibly from πηνέλοψ (“duck”).
penelope.a: Penelope, often used in reference to Homer's character, is a female first name of Greek origin. Its meaning is uncertain, but may derive from the Greek word penelops, which means duck or refers to another water fowl sacred to the Ancient Greeks.

penny.a: Penny is a feminine given name and nickname, often a short form (hypocorism) of Penelope.

percival.e: From Old French Perceval, name of a knight in a twelfth century Arthurian romance by the French poet Chrétien de Troyes. Shaped like Old French percier (“pierce”) + val (“valley”), but probably representing some or name, possibly related…
percival.a: Percival, also spelled Perceval, is a masculine given name derived from the Celtic name Peredur and likely influenced by the Old French percer, meaning pierce and val, meaning valley. The name was likely also influenced by the name Percy.

persephone.a: Persephone is an Ancient Greek feminine name used in reference to Persephone, the Greek goddess of spring and the Greek underworld.

peter.e: From Middle English Peter, from Old English Petrus, from Latin Petrus, from Ancient Greek Πέτρος, from πέτρος (“stone, rock”).
peter.a: Peter is a common masculine given name. It is derived directly from Greek Πέτρος, Petros , which itself was a translation of Aramaic Kefa ("stone, rock"), the new name Jesus gave to apostle Simon bar Jonah. An Old English variant is Piers.

peyton.a: Peyton is an English surname and a unisex given name. In Ireland it is known to have been among the anglicized forms of Ó Peatáin.

phelan.e: Reduced Anglicized form of Irish Ó Faoláin (“descendant of Faolán”), a hypocoristic form of faol (“wolf”).

phelim.a: Féilim or Feidhlim, is an Irish language masculine given name. The name is derived from the older form Feidhlimidh . Féilim has been variously anglicised as Felim, Phelim, Feilmy, Philip or Felix.

philip.e: From Middle English Philip, ultimately from Ancient Greek Φίλιππος, name of ancient kings of Macedonia, from φίλιππος (“fond of horses”), from φιλέω + ἵππος.
philip.a: Philip, also Phillip, is a male name derived from the Greek Φιλιππος (Philippos, lit. "horse-loving" or "fond of horses"), from a compound of φίλος (philos, "dear", "loved", "loving") and ἵππος (hippos, "horse").

philippa.e: A Latinate feminine form of Philip, recorded in medieval England, but originally pronounced like the masculine form.
philippa.a: Philippa is a feminine given name meaning "lover of horses" or "horses' friend", from the Greek Philippos, which is derived from philein, meaning to love and hippos, meaning horse. The English masculine form is Philip, which was formerly the vernacular form for both sexes.

phoebe.e: Latin Phoebē, from Ancient Greek Φοίβη, feminine form of Φοῖβος (“bright”).
phoebe.a: Phoebe or Phœbe is a female name, the feminine form of the male name Phoebus , an epithet of Apollo meaning "bright", "shining", and “pure”. In Greek mythology, Phoebe was a Titan associated with the power of prophecy as well as the moon. This was also an epithet of her granddaughter Artemis.

phoenix.e: From Latin phoenīx, Phoenīx, from Ancient Greek φοῖνῐξ, Φοῖνῐξ.
phoenix.a: Phoenix is a modern given name derived from the name for a mythological bird from Greek myth that has become a symbol of renewal, regeneration and immortality. It is a name in use for both boys and girls.

pia.a: Pia is a feminine given name. In Spanish, it is spelled Pía.

piper.a: Piper is an English given name meaning "piper". It is a transferred use of the surname, which originated as an occupational name in England in the Middle Ages for a pipe player.

pippa.a: Pippa is a feminine given name and a short form, usually of Philippa.

pixie.a: Pixie is a feminine given name of English origin.

pola.a: Pola is a feminine given name of Greek origin, a Polish and Spanish form of the name Apolonia, a feminine form of the ancient Greek name Apollinaris, a name derived from the Greek god Apollo.

polly.e: Nickname for Mary, created by rhyming with Molly.
polly.a: Polly is a given name, most often feminine, which originated as a variant of Molly (a diminutive of Mary). Polly may also be a short form of names such as Polina, Polona, Pauline, Paula, or Paulina.

poppy.a: Poppy is a feminine given name derived from the name of the flower poppy, itself derived from the Old English popæg and referring to various species of Papaver.

posie.a: Posy or Posey or Posie is an English given name derived from the English term for a small flower bouquet. A posy is also a word for a single flower. It can also be derived from an English nickname, sometimes used independently, for a formal name such as Josephine.

presley.e: The English surname is usually a variant of Priestley, from Old English prēost (“priest”) + lēah (“wood, clearing”). Equivalent to priest + -leigh.
presley.a: Presley is a surname and given name.

preston.e: From Old English Prēostatūn, from prēosta (“priests'”) + tūn (“settlement”).
preston.a: Preston is a masculine given name which may refer to:

primrose.e: The surname derives from a place name in Fife, Scotland; Watson (1926) derived this from /*prenn (“wood, tree”) + *rros (“moor, heath”). Taylor instead argued for Scottish Gaelic prím (“first”) + ros (“promontory”).
primrose.a: Primrose is an English feminine given name given in reference to the flower. The common name for the flower comes from the Latin phrase prima rosa, or first rose. It is also an English or Scottish surname.

prince.a: Prince is a masculine given name.

priscilla.e: Feminine diminutive form of a Roman cognomen Prīscus, from Latin prīscus (“former, ancient, old-fashioned”).
priscilla.a: Priscilla is an English female given name adopted from Latin Prisca, derived from priscus. The name first appears in the New Testament either as Priscilla or Prisca, a female leader in early Christianity.

priya.e: From Sanskrit प्रिया. Doublet of Frigg (and variants).
priya.a: Priya or Pria is a common given name in India which is also used in Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Thailand. It is cognate to the name of the Germanic goddess Frigg; both descend from the Proto-Indo-European stem *priH-o-, meaning "beloved".

qasim.a: Qasim, Kassem or Qasem is the transliteration of the male given name , pronounced with a long first syllable. The meaning is one who distributes. The first known bearer of the name was the son of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, Qasim ibn Muhammad.

quinn.e: The surname is Irish Ó Coinn (“descendant of Chief”).
quinn.a: Quinn is a unisex given name, derived from an Irish surname. Notable people with the given name include:

rachel.e: Rāchēl, from Ancient Greek Ῥαχήλ, from Biblical Hebrew רָחֵל (“ewe”).
rachel.a: Rachel is a feminine given name of Hebrew origin, popularized by the biblical figure Rachel, the wife of Israelite patriarch Jacob.

rae.a: Rae is a unisex given name. The Scottish name Rae is often associated with the Gaelic term "rath" which means "fortress." Rae is also the female variant of the Old High German Ray from regin meaning "counsel".

rafael.a: Rafael is a masculine given name. It is a Portuguese and Spanish form of the Hebrew name Raphael. It translates to "God has healed" and "God heals" in Hebrew.

rafe.a: Rafe is a given name for a male used in many countries across the world. If the name is English, Scandinavian or German it is of Old Norse origin (meaning "counsel of the wolf" or "wise wolf"), derived from the Old Norse Raðulfr through Old English Rædwulf.

rafi.a: Rafi is a male given name of Armenian and Arabic origin. It is one of the names of Allah, stemming from the Arabic verb rafaʿa , meaning "to lift, to raise (something high)". It is distinct from another male name, Rafi .

raheem.a: Rahim is an Arabic word meaning "Merciful", from the root R-Ḥ-M. Al-Rahim (the Merciful) is one of the attributes of God according to Islam. It is a male given name, sometimes a hypocorism for Abdu r-Raḥīm "Servant of the Merciful".

raiden.e: Possible a modern variant of Rayden, or a coinage rhyming with Braiden, Jaiden, etc.

raife.a: Raife is a masculine given name . It is an English, Scandinavian and German given name for a male, used in many countries across the world but most popular in English-speaking countries.

raine.a: Raine is a given name and surname derived from any of several personal names (such as Raymond or Lorraine). Notable people with the name include:

raisa.e: From the saint's name Раи́са, from Ancient Greek ῥήϊστος.
raisa.a: Raisa or Raissa is a female personal name. It is popular in Russia and South Asia (as a feminine form of Rais). It was also a historically typical female name amongst Jews of the Russian Empire, as a Hebrew and Yiddish origin variant.

ralph.e: From Middle English Radulf, from Old English Rǣdwulf (also as Raulf), from Proto-West Germanic *Rādawulf, from Proto-Germanic *Rēdawulfaz. Reinforced by similar forms brought to England, e.g.
ralph.a: Ralph is a male name of English origin, derived from the Old English Rædwulf and Old High German Radulf, cognate with the Old Norse Raðulfr . The most common forms are: Ralph, the common variant form in English, which takes either of the given pronunciations.

ralphie.a: Ralphie is a masculine given name, often a diminutive form (hypocorism) of Ralph.

raphael.e: From Latin Raphael, from Ῥᾱφᾱήλ, from Biblical Hebrew רָפָאֵל.
raphael.a: Raphael is a given name derived from the Hebrew rāp̄ā'ēl meaning "God has healed". Raphael is one of the archangels according to Abrahamic tradition.

raven.a: Raven is a given name in the English language. While it may be given to boys and girls, it is more frequently a feminine name. In the United States of America the name has ranked among the top 1,000 names given to baby girls since 1977.

ray.a: Ray is a given name and short form (hypocorism) of the given name Raymond and Rachel.

raya.a: Raya is a given name with multiple, unrelated origins in different cultures. It is a Bulgarian diminutive of Rayna, meaning happy or a Russian diminutive of Raisa, meaning rose. It might also be related to the Latin name Regina meaning queen.

rayan.a: Rayan , also spelt Rayyan, Rayyaan, Rayaan, Raian, Rayen, or Ryan is generally a male given name of Persian origin (and later) a male and female given name of Islamic/Arabic origin, meaning "luxuriant," "well-watered" or "satiated" in Arabic, while meaning "smart", "wise" or "thinker" in the…

raymond.e: From Old French Raimund, from *Raginmund, from Proto-Germanic *Raginamunduz, composed of *raginą + *mundō. Compare the first element in Reginald, Reynold, Ronald; the second element can be found in cognates Edmund, Sigmund, Osmond.
raymond.a: Raymond is a male given name of Germanic origin. It was borrowed into English from French (older French spellings were Reimund and Raimund, whereas the modern English and French spellings are identical). It originated as the Germanic ᚱᚨᚷᛁᚾᛗᚢᚾᛞ (Raginmund) or ᚱᛖᚷᛁᚾᛗᚢᚾᛞ (Reginmund).

rayna.a: Rayna is a feminine given name with multiple origins in diverse cultures. It can also be a middle name.

reagan.e: Anglicized from Gaelic Ó Riagáin (“descendant of Riagán”), a personal name possibly derived from ríodhgach (“impulsive, furious”), an alternative form of ríogach.
reagan.a: Reagan is a unisex given name, a transferred use of the Irish surnames Regan and Reagan, which are Anglicized forms of Ó Riagáin, meaning ‘’descendant of Riagáin’’, a name of uncertain meaning.

rebecca.e: The Vulgate () form of biblical Rebekah, from Hebrew רִבְקָה (“enchantingly beautiful, captivating, snare”).
rebecca.a: Rebecca or Rebekah is a feminine given name of Hebrew origin. It is the name of the biblical figure Rebecca, wife of Isaac and mother of Jacob and Esau.

reece.a: Reece is a given name and surname that derives from the Welsh name Rhys. Notable people with the name include:

reem.a: Reem is a feminine personal given name in Arabic meaning gazelle, which symbolizes purity and tenderness. It has been widely used in Arab poetry and literature as a symbol of a beautiful woman.

regan.a: Regan is a unisex given name with multiple origins. It is a transferred use of the Irish surnames Regan and Reagan, which are Anglicized forms of Ó Riagáin, meaning 'descendant of Riagán', a name of uncertain meaning.

reggie.a: Reggie is a given name, usually a short form of Reginald (male) or Regina (female).

reginald.e: From Latin Reginaldus, Latinization of names deriving from Proto-Germanic *Raginawaldaz.
reginald.a: Reginald is a masculine given name in the English language that derives from the Latin word for "king".

reilly.e: From Irish Ó Raghallaigh, a surname meaning "descendants of Raghallach".

reina.a: Reina, which is also spelled Raina, Rayna, or Reyna in English, is a feminine given name with multiple, unrelated origins from a number of different languages and cultures. All of these unrelated names are pronounced and written similarly in English.

remy.a: Rémy, Remy, Rémi, Remie, Rémie or Remi is a name of French origin meaning "oarsman", and is associated with the Latin name Remigius. It is used as either a surname or as a male or female given name. People with the name Remy include:

ren.a: Ren is a given name, most often Japanese.

renee.a: Renée (without the accent in non-French speaking countries) is a French feminine given name and surname. Renée is the female form of René, with the extra "e" making it feminine according to French grammar.

renzo.a: Renzo, the diminutive of Lorenzo, is an Italian masculine given name and a surname.

reuben.a: Reuben or Reuven is a Biblical male first name from Hebrew רְאוּבֵן (Re'uven), meaning "behold, a son". In the Bible, Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob.

rex.a: Rex is a male given name, short for Rexford or Reginald, derived from the Latin word rex, meaning "king". This is the etymological root word for king in several languages.

rhea.a: Rhea is a given name and surname. As a given name, it is generally pronounced , and was originally the name of Rhea, a Titan in Greek mythology. As a surname, it is generally pronounced (; RAY), and is of Scottish origin.

rhys.a: Rhys or Rhŷs is a popular Welsh given name (usually male) that is famous in Welsh history and is also used as a surname. It originates from Deheubarth, an old region of South West Wales, with famous kings such as Rhys ap Tewdwr.

ria.a: Ria is a feminine given name of multiple origins. In Western countries, it is often a short form of Maria. Ria is also an Indonesian name meaning joy or hilarity.

riaan.a: Riaan is a generally male given name, popular in South Africa. The name can mean "little king". It is also a Hindu male given name.

richard.a: Richard is a masculine given name. It originates, via Old French, from Old Frankish and is a compound of the words descending from Proto-Germanic *rīk- 'ruler, leader, king' and *hardu- 'strong, brave, hardy', and it therefore means 'strong in rule'.

richie.a: Richie or Richy is a masculine given name or short form (hypocorism) of Richard. It is also a surname. Notable people with the name include:

rico.a: Rico is a diminutive of either the Spanish masculine given name Federico or Ricardo, or of the Italian given name Enrico. Rico can also be a nickname or a surname. Notable people with the name include:

rio.a: Rio is a unisex give name which may refer to:

rita.e: From Rita. A shortening of Italian Margherita, and Spanish Margarita, cognates of English Margaret. An Italian Saint Rita was canonized in 1900. The English name came into regular use in early twentieth century.
rita.a: Rita is a female name, often a name in its own right, but mostly a shortened version of Margarita. The feast day of Rita is generally celebrated on May 22 in honor of Saint Rita of Cascia.

river.a: River is a given name of English origin taken from river, the English word for a naturally flowing watercourse. It is in common use in English-speaking countries such as the United States for both males and females.

riya.a: Riya is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Riya, Japanese singer Riya Bamniyal, Indian actress Riya Deepsi, Indian actress and model Riya Sen (born 1981), Indian actress Riya Suman, Indian actress Riya Vishwanathan, Indian actress

roan.a: Roan is a Frisian given name. It is sometimes used also in other languages such as English, where it can be also an alternate form of Rowan. It can be also a surname.

robert.e: From Anglo-Norman Robert, from the Old cognate of Old High German Hrodperht (normalised form: Ruodberht), from Proto-West Germanic *Hrōþiberht, from Proto-Germanic *Hrōþiberhtaz.
robert.a: The name Robert is an ancient Germanic given name, from Proto-Germanic *Hrōþi- "fame" and *berhta- "bright" (Hrōþiberhtaz). Compare Old Dutch Robrecht and Old High German Hrodebert . It is the second most frequently used given name of ancient Germanic origin.

robin.a: Robin is a unisex given name and a surname. It was originally a diminutive masculine given name or nickname of Robert, derived from the prefix Ro- (Old Frankish: hrod, meaning 'fame' and berht, meaning 'bright'), and the suffix -in (Old French diminutive).

robyn.a: Robyn is a unisex given name. Robin is a variant which is also used in both genders. It is of Germanic origin and means 'bright famous one'.

rocco.e: From the form of the name of 14th century saint Roch, of origin. The meaning is obscure; Old High German hruoh (“crow”) (from Proto-Germanic *hrōkaz), hrok (“rest”) (modern Ruhe) and rohōn (“to roar”) (modern röhren) have been suggested.
rocco.a: Rocco or Rocko is both a given name and a surname. Rocco is a masculine name of Italian origin. It is thought to derive from the Old German word "hrok", which means to rest or repose.

rohan.e: Habitational surname from Rohan in Morbihan, Brittany. Also a variant.
rohan.a: Rohan is both a given name and a surname. It has multiple origins, including Arabic, Persian, Indian, Irish and Scottish Gaelic, and Japanese. In Arabic, it means "spiritual." In Persian, Rohan means good character and piety.

roisin.a: Róisín, sometimes anglicized as Roisin or Rosheen, is an Irish female given name, meaning "little rose". The English equivalent is Rose, Rosaleen or Rosie.

roma.a: Roma is a unisex given name in many languages, and is the feminine form of the name Roman in some languages. In Italian, it is a toponymic name that stems from the city of Rome.

roman.e: From Old French Romain, from Latin Rōmānus. Displaced native Romish.
roman.a: Roman is a masculine given name meaning from Rome, which originated within the Roman Empire, via Latin. In its initial sense, the title "Roman", denotes a member of the Roman Empire, or belonging to or identifying with Roman (or Byzantine) culture.

romeo.e: Italian Romeo, from Ancient Greek Ῥωμαῖος (“Roman”).
romeo.a: Romeo is an Italian masculine given name. It arose from the Greek Ρωμαίος for a Roman citizen or a pilgrim to Rome.

romi.a: Romi is a given name and may refer to: Romi Dames (born 1979), Japanese-American actress Romi Garduce (born 1969), Filipino mountain climber and IT Professional in Procter and Gamble Philippines Romi Goldmuntz , Belgian businessman who played an essential role in the survival of the diamond…

romilly.a: Romilly is a unisex given name, a transferred use of an English surname derived from the French place name Romilly.

romy.a: Romy is a given name, often a diminutive form of names such as Rosemary or Romina, Romilda, Romana, Roman or Romeo. People with the name include:

ronald.e: Anglicized from Scottish Gaelic Raghnall, itself derived from Old Norse Rǫgnvaldr, from rǫgn (“advice”) + valdr (“power”), later partly merged with the Continental Germanic equivalent Reynold.
ronald.a: Ronald is a masculine given name derived from the Old Norse Rögnvaldr, or possibly from Old English Regenweald. In some cases Ronald is an Anglicised form of the Gaelic Raghnall, a name likewise derived from Rögnvaldr.

ronan.a: Rónán, anglicised as Ronan, is an Irish and Breton male given name and surname derived from rón, the Irish word for 'seal'. The given name dates back to Primitive Irish in the form ᚏᚑᚅᚐᚅᚅ [ᚋᚐᚊ ᚉᚑᚋᚑᚌᚐᚅᚅ] (RONANN [MAQ COMOGANN]), found as an ogham inscription which translates as 'Rónán, son of…

ronnie.a: Ronnie is a given name and a surname. It can be a pet form of the masculine name Ronald and the feminine name Veronica. The masculine Ronald is derived from the Old Norse Rögnvaldr, which is composed of the elements regin ("advice", "decision") and valdr ("ruler").

rooney.a: Rooney is the given name or common first name of the following people: Rooney Lee , an American planter, military general and politician. Rooney Mara (born 1985), an American actress. Rooney Massara (born 1943), a British rower and businessman.

rory.e: Anglicized form of Scottish Gaelic Ruairidh and Irish Ruairí (“red-haired king”), from Old Irish Ruaidrí (“red king”).
rory.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

rosa.a: Rosa is a female given name, especially in the Spanish, Portuguese, and Italian languages.

rosaleen.e: Anglicized from Irish Róisín, a diminutive of Rose.
rosaleen.a: Rosaleen is an Irish female first name. It is an Anglicized version of the Irish name Róisín, the diminutive of "rose" in the Irish language; it therefore means "little rose". It has use in Ireland since the 16th century, possibly popularised by Rosaline in Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet.

rosalie.e: From French Rosalie, from the saints’ name Rosālia, from rosa (“rose”).
rosalie.a: Rosalie is a feminine given name, the French, German, and Dutch form of the Roman name Rosalia, which was ultimately derived from the Latin word rosa, meaning rose. The name may also be spelled Rozalie in Dutch and Rosalee or Rosaleigh in English.

roscoe.e: From a place in Lancashire, from Old Norse rá (“roebuck”) + skógr (“forest”).

rose.a: Rose is a female given name. It is a late Latin name derived from rosa, meaning "rose". Variants are Rosa, Rosario, Rosie, Rosalba, Rosalie, Rosalia, Rosina, Rosaria, Rosalyn and Rosalina.

rosemary.e: A combination of Rose + Mary, referring to the flower as a symbol of Virgin Mary, first recorded in the eighteenth century. It is found in continental Europe as Rosemarie and Rosa Maria.
rosemary.a: Rosemary is a feminine given name, a combination of the names Rose which is a flower that belongs to the Rose family, and from the name Mary which is the name of the Virgin Mary and means Strong, Fertile. It can also be used in reference to the herb named rosemary.

rosie.a: Rosie is a feminine given name of English origin. It can be a diminutive form of the English language given name Rose, which is of Latin origin. Similar diminutives in other languages include: Rosa becoming Rosita in Spanish, and Ruža becoming Ružica in Slavic languages.

ross.a: Ross is an English-language name derived from Gaelic, most commonly used in Scotland. It is also the name of a county in the highland area (Ross and Cromarty). It can be used as a given name, typically for males, but is also a typical family name for people of Scottish descent (Clan Ross).

rowan.e: Anglicised from the saints' name Ruadhán (“little red one”), or as a surname from Ó Ruadháin (“descendant of Ruadhán”).
rowan.a: Rowan () is a traditionally masculine Irish given name and surname, now also in use as a given name for girls. Variants of the name include Roan, Rohan, Ruadhán, and Ruadh.
