rowen.a: Rowen is both a surname and male given name. Notable people with the name include:

roy.e: From various sources: * Anglo-Norman roy (“king”) a variant of Old French roi, from Latin rēx, rēgem from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵs (“ruler, king”).
roy.a: Roy is both a given name and a family surname with varied origins.

ruaidhri.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

ruairi.e: From Old Irish Ruaidrí. Cognate with Scottish Gaelic Ruairidh and Manx Ruaree.
ruairi.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

ruairidh.e: From Old Irish Ruaidrí. Cognate to Irish Ruairí and Manx Ruaree.
ruairidh.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

ruari.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

ruaridh.a: Rory is a given name of Gaelic origin. It is an anglicisation of the Irish: Ruairí/Ruaidhrí and Scottish Gaelic: Ruairidh/Ruaraidh and is common to the Irish, Highland Scots and their diasporas. The meaning of the name is "red king", composed of ruadh ("red") and rígh ("king").

ruben.a: Reuben or Reuven is a Biblical male first name from Hebrew רְאוּבֵן (Re'uven), meaning "behold, a son". In the Bible, Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob.

ruby.e: The female name derives from ruby in the 19th century. The programming language was named after the gemstone.
ruby.a: Ruby is a predominantly feminine given name taken from the name of the gemstone ruby. The name of the gemstone comes from the Latin rubinus, meaning red. The ruby is the birthstone for the month of July.

rudi.a: Rudy or Rudi is a masculine given name, sometimes short for Rudolf, Rudolph, Rawad, Rudra, Ruairidh, or variations thereof, a nickname and a surname which may refer to:

rudy.a: Rudy or Rudi is a masculine given name, sometimes short for Rudolf, Rudolph, Rawad, Rudra, Ruairidh, or variations thereof, a nickname and a surname which may refer to:

rueben.a: Reuben or Reuven is a Biblical male first name from Hebrew רְאוּבֵן (Re'uven), meaning "behold, a son". In the Bible, Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob.

rufus.a: Rufus is a masculine given name, a surname, an Ancient Roman cognomen and a nickname (from Latin rufus, "red"). Notable people with the name include:

rupert.e: A name, brought to England by Prince Rupert of the Rhine in the seventeenth century. The geometry sense is also a reference to Prince Rupert, who posed the question of whether a cube could be passed through a hole made in another cube of…

ruqayyah.a: Ruqayya is an Arabic female given name meaning "to rise”, or ”she who rises high”. Like most Arabic names, it has multiple transliterations: Ruqayyah, Ruqiya, Ruqaya, Ruqaiya, Rukayya, Rukaiya, Rukiya, Rakiya, Rakia, etc..

ruth.e: From Ruth the Moabite, Hebrew רות, of uncertain origin, possibly meaning "companion". Also associated with the English noun ruth (“compassion”) by Puritans.
ruth.a: Ruth is a common female given name, noted from Ruth, the eponymous heroine of the Book of Ruth.

ryan.a: Ryan is an English-language given name of Irish origin. Traditionally a male name, it has been used increasingly for both boys and girls since the 1970s.

ryder.a: Ryder is both a surname and masculine given name. Notable people with the name include:

saad.a: Saad is a common male Arabic given name. The name stems from the Arabic verb sa‘ada . Saad is the stem of variant given names Suad and Sa‘id.

sabrina.a: Sabrina is a feminine given name derived from Proto-Celtic *Sabrinā.

sadhbh.e: From Middle Irish Sadb, from Old Irish Sadb, from Proto-Celtic *swadwā, feminine derivative of *swādus (“sweet”).
sadhbh.a: Sadhbh is an Irish feminine personal name.

sadie.a: Sadie is a feminine given name which originated as an English diminutive of the Hebrew name Sarah. It has long been used as an independent name. It is also a hypocorism of Sara or Sarah, and on rare occasions a masculine nickname.

sage.a: Sage () is a family name and a given name. It can also be spelled Saige or Sayge or Sayje. Sage's origin, as well as its use, is in the English language.

salma.a: Salma is an Arabic feminine name that means "peace.” It comes from the Arabic word Salam.

sam.a: Sam is a unisex given name. It is often short for other names, such as Samuel or Samantha.

samantha.e: It was recorded in the 17th century in England.
samantha.a: Samantha is an English feminine given name in use since the 17th century that is of uncertain derivation. It is now in popular use worldwide due to various popular culture influences.

sami.e: From Sápmi, from one of the languages, of uncertain origin/meaning, but possibly related to *źémijāˀ (“land”). Displaced native Old English Finn (the direct descendant is Finn (“person from Finland”)). More at Sápmi and Sami.
sami.a: Sami, also Sammy or Samy, is a given name and surname of different origins and meanings, most prevalent in the Arab world and Scandinavia.

samir.a: Samir (also spelled Sameer) is a masculine given name of multiple origins. In Arabic, Samir means "holy", "jovial", "loyal", or "charming". In Albanian, it literally means "so good" but loosely "exquisite", "superb", or "perfect".

samson.e: From Middle English Sampson, Sampsoun, Samson, from Latin Samson, from Ancient Greek Σαμψών, from Hebrew שִׁמְשׁוֹן.
samson.a: Samson can be either a masculine given name or a surname. It may refer to the following people:

samuel.e: From Latin Samuēl, from Ancient Greek Σαμουήλ, from Biblical Hebrew שְׁמוּאֵל.
samuel.a: Samuel is a male name and a surname of Hebrew origin. It means "name of God", deriving from the Hebrew Shem (which means "name") + ʾĒl (which means "God" or "deity").

santiago.a: Santiago is a masculine Spanish name that derives from the Hebrew name Jacob (Ya'akov) via "Sant Iago", "Sant Yago", "Santo Iago", or "Santo Yago", first used to denote Saint James the Great, the brother of John the Apostle.

santino.a: Santino is an Italian masculine given name or nickname, meaning “little saint” in Italian. It is a diminutive version of the given name Santo, meaning “saint” or “holy”. The name is highly popular in Argentina, the United States, and its native Italy.

saoirse.a: Saoirse is an Irish-language given name meaning "freedom". It became popular in Ireland in the late 20th century. The actress Saoirse Ronan has given the name prominence internationally since her 2007 breakthrough in Atonement.

sara.a: Sarah is a common feminine given name of Hebrew origin. It derives its popularity from the biblical matriarch Sarah, the wife of Abraham and a major figure in the Abrahamic religions.

sarah.e: From Biblical Hebrew שָׂרָה (“lady, princess”), from the Biblical figure originally named Sarai (שָׂרָי).
sarah.a: Sarah is a common feminine given name of Hebrew origin. It derives its popularity from the biblical matriarch Sarah, the wife of Abraham and a major figure in the Abrahamic religions.

sasha.e: Borrowed from the diminutive form of Alexander and Alexandra; in English mostly from Russian Са́ша, a diminutive form for both Алекса́ндр (“Alexander”) and Алекса́ндра (“Alexandra”).

saskia.a: Saskia is a Dutch feminine given name of uncertain origin. It has been in use since the Middle Ages and is also in occasional use in the Anglosphere. One source word might be the Germanic sachs, meaning Saxon.

saul.a: Saul is a masculine given name of Hebrew origin. It is the English form of שָׁאוּל‎, the Hebrew name of the Biblical King Saul. The name translates to "asked for/borrowed".

savannah.e: The cities are named after the Savannah River, possibly derived from.
savannah.a: Savannah or Savanna is a feminine given name, taken from either the name of the city of Savannah, Georgia, or savanna, a large, grassy plain ecosystem. The name has been among the 1,000 most popular names for newborn American girls since 1983 and among the top 100 since 1993.

scarlett.a: Scarlett is a feminine given name. It gained popularity due to the character Scarlett O'Hara in Margaret Mitchell's best-selling novel Gone with the Wind and the film adaptation. The name has been well used in recent years for girls in the United Kingdom and in the United States.

scott.a: Scott is a male name of Scottish origin. Notable people and fictional characters with the name include:

seamus.a: Séamus is an Irish male given name, of Hebrew origin via Latin. It is the Irish equivalent of the name James. The name James is the English New Testament variant for the Hebrew name Jacob.

sean.e: Borrowed from Old French Jehan, from Latin Iōhannēs, from Ancient Greek Ἰωάννης, contraction from Hebrew יוֹחָנָן.
sean.a: Sean, also spelled Seán (or sometimes Séan) in Hiberno-English, is a male given name of Irish and English origin.

seana.a: Seana or Seána is a female given name.

seanie.a: Seánie or Seanie is a given name. Notable people with the name include: Seánie Barry (born 1945), Irish hurler Seánie Duggan , Irish hurler Seánie McGrath (born 1975), Irish hurler Seánie McMahon (born 1972), Irish hurler Seánie O'Leary (born 1952), Irish hurler

sebastian.e: From Latin Sebastiānus, name of an early Christian saint, from ancient city of Sebaste in Asia Minor (modern Sivas, Turkey), from Ancient Greek Σεβαστός (“august, venerable, exalted”), itself a translation of the Roman title Augustus.
sebastian.a: Sebastian or Sebastiæn is both a given name and a surname.

selena.e: Either a variant of Selina, from Latin Caelīna (“heavenly”), or from Selene, the goddess of the moon.
selena.a: Selena () is a feminine given name, a probable variant of Selene, the goddess and personification of the Moon in Greek mythology and religion.

selina.e: First recorded in England in the 17th century, possibly from Latin Caelīna (“heavenly”), or a variant of Selene, the goddess of the moon.
selina.a: Selina () is a feminine given name, considered either a variant of Selene, the goddess and personification of the Moon in Greek mythology and religion, or a spelling variation of the name Celina, which is derived from the Roman name Cecilia, referring to a woman from the Caecilia gens.

seoirse.e: From Georges, from Latin Geōrgius, from Ancient Greek Γεώργιος.
seoirse.a: Seoirse is an Irish masculine given name. It is the Irish equivalent of George. The name was rare in Ireland prior to the ascension of the House of Hanover to the throne of the Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland in the early 18th century.

seosamh.e: Borrowed from Old French Joseph, from Latin Iōsēphus, from Ancient Greek Ἰωσήφ, Ἰώσηπος, from Hebrew יוֹסֵף.
seosamh.a: Joseph is a common male name, derived from the Hebrew Yosef . "Joseph" is used, along with "Josef", mostly in English, French and partially German languages. This spelling is also found as a variant in the languages of the modern-day Nordic countries. In Portuguese and Spanish, the name is "José".

seren.a: Seren is a given name in Welsh, and both a given name and surname in Turkish. In Welsh, it is a female and male name meaning "star".

serena.e: From the name of an early Christian saint, Latin serena (“serene”).
serena.a: Serena is a feminine given name. It is derived from the Latin word serēnus, meaning "clear, tranquil, serene". This name was borne by one of the first saints, Serena of Rome, purported wife of Emperor Diocletian.

seth.e: Ancient Greek Σήθ, from Biblical Hebrew שֵׁת.
seth.a: Seth is a masculine given name, tracing its origin to the biblical figure Seth, the third son of Adam and Eve. The English form is derived from the Greek Σήθ , ultimately from the Hebrew שֵׁת .

shane.e: Anglicized form of the Northern Irish pronunciation of Irish Seán, from Old French Jehan, from Latin Johannes, variant of Ioannes, from Ἰωάννης, from Hebrew יוֹחָנָן.
shane.a: Shane is a masculine given name. It is an anglicized version of the Irish male name Séaghan/Séan, which itself is cognate to the name John. Shane comes from the way the name Seán is pronounced in the Ulster dialect of the Irish language, as opposed to Shaun or Shawn.

shauna.e: From Shaun + a, variant of Irish Seán, from Old French Jehan, from Latin Johannes, variant of Ioannes, from Ἰωάννης, from Hebrew יוֹחָנָן.
shauna.a: Shauna is an Irish female given name. It is the female version of the male names Shawn or Sean, both of which are in turn derived from John.

shay.e: Variant of Shea, from Irish Ó Séaghdha.

sheila.e: Anglicized spelling of Irish Síle, equivalent to Caelia.
sheila.a: Sheila (alternatively spelled Shelagh, Sheilagh and Sheelagh) is a common feminine given name, derived from the Irish name Síle, which is believed to be a Gaelic form of the Latin name Caelia, the feminine form of the Roman clan name Caelius, meaning 'heavenly'.

shelby.e: From a medieval name, of origin, yet likely an alteration of Middle English Selby, Salibi (“dweller of the willow place”), from salwe (“willow, sallow”) + -by.
shelby.a: Shelby is a given name, a transferred use of the northern English surname. Its meaning is uncertain. It has been in use as a given name, mainly in North America, since the 1700s.

sheridan.e: As a surname, from Irish Ó Sirideáin.
sheridan.a: Sheridan is a unisex given name of Irish origin.

shiloh.a: Shiloh, Shylo or Shilo is a unisex given name.

sidney.e: From Old English *Sīdaneġ, the name of a place in Surrey, from sīd (“wide”) + eġ (“island”).
sidney.a: Sidney (often shortened to Sid) is an English given name derived from the surname, which itself has two different derivations depending on the origins of the family: in some cases a place name, itself from Old English, meaning "wide water meadow", and in others from the French place name "St Denis".

sidra.a: Sidra is a given name of Latin origin meaning "Goddess of the stars" or "like a star". The name Sidra is also an Islamic name, short for Sidrat al-Muntaha, a holy tree at the end of the seventh heaven. Notable people with the name include:

sienna.a: Sienna or Siena is a feminine given name of Italian origin and unclear meaning. The original usage of the name is derived from the Italian city and may also refer to the burnt orange color of its clay rooftops. Roman Catholics have sometimes used the name in honor of Saint Catherine of Siena.

sierra.a: Sierra is both a surname and a feminine given name. It is the Spanish word for saw or mountain range. It originates from the Galicia and Asturias regions of northern Spain.

silas.e: From Latin Sīlās, from Ancient Greek Σίλας, from שְׁאִילָא, cognate of Hebrew שָׁאוּל (“Saul”).
silas.a: Silas is a common given name and a lesser-known surname. It is a cognate of Silvanus.

sile.e: From Middle Irish Síle, from Anglo-Norman Cecile, from Latin Caecilia.
sile.a: Síle is a feminine Irish language given name, from which the anglicised form Sheila is derived.

simon.e: From Middle English Simon, Symond, Symounde, from Anglo-Norman Simon, Simond, Simund, a conflation of two unrelated names: one from Latin Simon, from Σίμων, strictly from likely σῑμός (“snub-nosed”)but used for Biblical Hebrew שִׁמְעוֹן
simon.a: Simon is a given name, from Hebrew שִׁמְעוֹן Šimʻôn, meaning "listen" or "hearing". It is also a classical Greek name, deriving from an adjective meaning "flat-nosed". In the first century AD, Simon was the most popular male name for Jews in Roman Judea.

sinead.a: Sinéad is an Irish feminine name. It is derived from the French Jeanette, which is cognate to the English Janet, itself a feminine form of the Hebrew Yohanan, "God forgave/God gratified". In English, Sinéad is also commonly spelled Sinead.

siobhan.e: From earlier Sibán, from Anglo-Norman Jehane or Jehanne, from Old French Jehanne, from Johanna, variant of Joanna, from Ἰωάννα, from Hebrew יוֹחָנָה, the feminized form of יְהוֹחָנָן or יוֹחָנָן, which produced John and its many doublets.
siobhan.a: Siobhán is a female name of Irish origin. The most common anglicisations are Siobhan , Shavawn, Shebahn, Shauvan, Shevaun and Shivaun. A now uncommon spelling variant is Siubhán.

siofra.a: Síofra is a feminine given name of Irish origin meaning elf or changeling.

sive.a: Sadhbh is an Irish feminine personal name.

sky.e: From sky. As a surname, a translation of German Himmel and an anglicization of Ashkenazic surnames ending in -sky.

skye.e: Derived from Scottish Gaelic An t-Eilean Sgitheanach, of long disputed (probably non-Indo-European) origin, with several theories proposed and none widely accepted; see Etymology of Skye.
skye.a: Skye is both a given name and surname.

skylar.a: Skyler or Skylar () is a unisex given name, an Anglicized spelling of the surname and given name Schuyler. Schuyler was introduced into America as a surname by 17th-century Dutch settlers arriving in New York.

skyler.a: Skyler or Skylar () is a unisex given name, an Anglicized spelling of the surname and given name Schuyler. Schuyler was introduced into America as a surname by 17th-century Dutch settlers arriving in New York.

sloane.a: Sloane or Sloan is a given name, a transferred use of the Irish surname Ó Sluaghadháin, meaning "descendant of Sluaghadhán". Sluaghadhán is an Irish diminutive form of the Irish name Sluaghadh, which means expedition or raid.

sofia.e: Variant spelling of Sophia and from various other languages' own adaptations of Ancient Greek Σοφία (“wisdom, especially divine wisdom”).
sofia.a: Sophia, also spelled Sofia, is a feminine given name, from the Greek personification of wisdom . Other forms include Sophie, Sofiya, Sofija, Sophy, Sophea, and Sofie.

sol.a: Sol is a given name, usually a form of "Solomon" or a gender-neutral Spanish name meaning "sun." Notable people with the name include: Sol Aragones (born 1977), Filipina broadcast journalist and politician Sol Bamba (born 1985), French-born Ivorian footballer Sol Bloom , member of the U.S.

solomon.e: From Latin Solomōn (variant of Salomon), from Ancient Greek Σολομών, from Biblical Hebrew שְׁלֹמֹה, from שָׁלוֹם (“peace”).
solomon.a: Solomon is a masculine given name and surname of Hebrew origin, popularized by the biblical figure Solomon, Israelite monarch and son of David. The name is derived from the Latin Solomōn, borrowed from the Ancient Greek Solomṓn , ultimately from the Hebrew Šĕlōmō .

somhairle.e: From Old Norse Sumarliði, from sumar (“summer”) + liði (“one who goes, fares”).
somhairle.a: Sorley and Somerled are masculine given names in the English language, Anglicizations of Scottish Gaelic Somhairle and Norse Sumarlidi.

sonny.a: Sonny is a common nickname and occasional given name.

sophia.e: Chiefly from Latin Sophia, from Ancient Greek Σοφία, from σοφία (“wisdom”), especially in reference to holy or divine wisdom under the influence of Biblical Hebrew חוכמה, to the early martyr St.
sophia.a: Sophia, also spelled Sofia, is a feminine given name, from the Greek personification of wisdom . Other forms include Sophie, Sofiya, Sofija, Sophy, Sophea, and Sofie.

sophie.a: Sophie is a feminine given name, from the Greek word for 'wisdom'.

soraya.e: Borrowed from ثریا, from ثریا (“brilliant gem; Pleiades”), ultimately from Arabic ثُرَيَّا.
soraya.a: Soraya is a feminine Arabic and Persian name. It is derived from the Arabic name for the Pleiades star cluster, Thurayyā or Suraya . The name, also spelled Zoraya, is used in Spain and throughout the Spanish-speaking world with an origin in Al-Andalus.

sorcha.e: From sorcha (“bright, clear, conspicuous”), from Old Irish sorchae (“bright, luminous”).
sorcha.a: Sorcha is a Gaelic feminine given name. It is common to both the Irish and Scottish Gaelic languages, and is derived from the Old Irish word sorchae, soirche meaning "brightness".

sorley.e: From Scottish Gaelic Somhairle, from Old Norse Sumarliði.
sorley.a: Sorley and Somerled are masculine given names in the English language, Anglicizations of Scottish Gaelic Somhairle and Norse Sumarlidi.

spencer.e: An occupational surname from Spenser, Spencer, Spensier, from the common noun spenser (“spencer”), denoting someone who works in a spense (“spence”), or as a butler or steward.
spencer.a: Spencer is a given name of British origin that means "steward" or "administrator".

stanley.e: From places in England, Old English stān (“stone”) + lēah (“meadow”). Equivalent to stone + -leigh. * The given name has also been used as an anglicisation of Stanisław, Stanislav and related names.
stanley.a: Stanley is a toponymic surname, a contraction of stan (a form of "stone") and leigh (meadow), later also being used as a masculine given name.

stefan.e: From Ancient Greek στεφανίζω (“to crown”) & Ancient Greek στέφανος (“that which surrounds, crown, wreath”).
stefan.a: Stefan is a masculine given name, a form of the English name Stephen. Variants include Ștefan, Štefan and Stefán.

stefania.a: Stefania [in all languages except for Italian and Polish pronounced like Ste-pha-nee-ah] is a female name in Belarusian, Bulgarian, Croatian, Czech, Greek, Stefánia Hungarian, Italian, Romanian, Polish, Serbian, Macedonian, Slovak, Slovene, Ukrainian and Russian, originating from Old Greek meaning…

stella.a: Stella is a female given name. It is derived from the Latin word for star. It has been in use in English-speaking countries since it was first used by Philip Sidney in Astrophel and Stella, his 1580s sonnet sequence.

stephanie.e: French Stéphanie. The standard English feminine form of Stephen.
stephanie.a: Stephanie or Stefanie is a feminine name that comes from the Greek name Στέφανος (Stephanos) meaning "wreath, garland, christmas wreath or crown".

stephen.e: From Latin Stephanus, from Ancient Greek Στέφανος, from στέφανος (“crown, wreath”), from στέφω (“to put round, to surround”).
stephen.a: Stephen or Steven is an English male first name. It is particularly significant to Christians, as it belonged to Saint Stephen , an early disciple and deacon who, according to the Book of Acts, was stoned to death; he is widely regarded as the first martyr (or "protomartyr") of the Christian Church.

steven.e: Middle English Stevene, Steven, from Anglo-Norman Estievne, Estievene, from Latin Stephanus, from Ancient Greek Στέφανος, from στέφανος (“crown, wreath”), from στέφω (“to put round, to surround”).
steven.a: Stephen or Steven is an English male first name. It is particularly significant to Christians, as it belonged to Saint Stephen , an early disciple and deacon who, according to the Book of Acts, was stoned to death; he is widely regarded as the first martyr (or "protomartyr") of the Christian Church.

stevie.a: Stevie is a unisex given name, usually a short form (hypocorism) of Stephen, Steven, Stephanie and other names, and occasionally a nickname.

storm.a: Storm is a unisex given name. Notable people with the given name include:

subhan.a: Subhan or Sobhan is masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin meaning "praise, exalted, glory". Notable people with the name include:

sultan.a: Sultan is a male given name and surname

summer.a: Summer is an English feminine given name of recent coinage derived from the word for the season of summer, the warmest season of the year and a time people generally associate with carefree and fun activities. It has been in common use as a name since at least 1970 in English-speaking countries.

sunny.a: Sunny is a unisex name. It can be a given name, a surname, and a nickname, especially from names such as: Sana, Sunil, Sundeep, Sunita, Shams Suniel, or Suraj. Notable people with the name include:

sydney.e: For the surname and given name, see Sidney. The cities in Australia and Canada are named after British politician Thomas Townshend, 1st Viscount Sydney (1733–1800).

syeda.e: Arabic سَيِّدَة. * From سیدہ, from Arabic سَيِّدَة

sylvia.a: Sylvia is a feminine given name of Latin origin. The French form is Sylvie. The name originates from the Latin word for forest Silva and its meaning is spirit of the wood.

szymon.a: Szymon is a Polish version of the masculine given name Simon.

tabitha.e: From טביתא (“doe, roe, gazelle”), translated as Dorcas in the Bible.
tabitha.a: Tabitha is an English feminine given name, originating with (or made popular through) Tabitha (Dorcas), mentioned in the New Testament Acts 9:36.

tadgh.a: Tadhg, also Taḋg , commonly anglicized as "Taig" or "Teague", is an Irish and Scottish Gaelic masculine name that was very common when the Goidelic languages predominated, to the extent that it is a synecdoche for Irish-speaking man. The name signifies "poet" or "philosopher".

tadhg.e: From Middle Irish Tadg (whence also Old Norse Taðkr), from the common noun tadg (“poet”), from pre-Goidelic *tazgos, from Proto-Celtic *taskos (“badger”). Cognate with Manx Taig and with names like Tasgetius, Tasciovanus, Moritasgus.
tadhg.a: Tadhg, also Taḋg , commonly anglicized as "Taig" or "Teague", is an Irish and Scottish Gaelic masculine name that was very common when the Goidelic languages predominated, to the extent that it is a synecdoche for Irish-speaking man. The name signifies "poet" or "philosopher".

tahlia.a: Talia is a Modern Hebrew feminine given name, as well as a variant spelling of Thalia and a short form of Natalia. Jews interpret it as a Hebrew combination of ṭal ('dew') and the theophoric suffix -yāh, meaning 'dew of God'.

tala.a: Tala is a female or unisex name that can be found in various ethnic groups. Many people share this name, but its meaning and background varies depending on the culture and language. In Persian, Tala is a female given name meaning gold.

talha.a: Talha or Thalha is an Arabic masculine given name, meaning "fruitful tree from heaven". Talha is the name of a well-known sahabi (companion) of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, Talha ibn Ubayd Allah. He is renowned for saving Muhammad's face from an arrow by holding his hand in the way.

talia.a: Talia is a Modern Hebrew feminine given name, as well as a variant spelling of Thalia and a short form of Natalia. Jews interpret it as a Hebrew combination of ṭal ('dew') and the theophoric suffix -yāh, meaning 'dew of God'.

tallulah.e: Tallulah, name of a river in Georgia. See etymology section of Wikipedia article Tallulah River.

tamara.e: Of Slavic origin, mainly from Russian Тама́ра, name of a 12th-century saint in the Eastern Orthodox Church, cognate with English biblical Tamar, from Hebrew תמר (“date palm”).
tamara.a: Tamara is a variant of the Hebrew feminine given name Tamar, a biblical name. The variant originated in the Russian language and spread into other languages through Russian.

tara.e: Irish Teamhrach, genitive of Teamhair, from Old Irish Temair. The female given name is derived from the name of the plantation in Gone with the Wind, named for the place in Ireland.
tara.a: Tara is a given name with multiple meanings in different cultures. In Ireland, it is derived from the Hill of Tara, an archaeological site located near the River Boyne in County Meath, which according to tradition was the seat of the High King of Ireland.

taran.a: Taran is both a given name and surname, of different origins. It may be writing without diacritics the Romanian surname Țăran .Notable people with the name include:

tate.e: From Middle English *Tate, partially from Old English Tāta, from Proto-West Germanic *tait, from Proto-Germanic *taitaz (“radiant, glad, cheerful, tender”); and partially from Old Norse Táta, a personal name of unknown meaning.
tate.a: Tate is an English gender-neutral given name and nickname.

taylor.a: Taylor is a unisex given name mainly in use in English-speaking countries and especially in the United States. Variants include Tayla and Taylah; both are feminine and most popular in Australia and New Zealand, whose non-rhotic accents mean that they are pronounced the same as "Taylor".

teagan.a: Teagan is a surname and Irish unisex given name that means 'attractive', 'beautiful' or 'perfect'.

teague.e: From the first name Tadhg. Cognate with English taig (“A Catholic”). Compare Mick and Paddy.

ted.a: Ted is a masculine given name. It is usually a diminutive form (hypocorism) for Edward, Edwin, Edgar, Edmund, Theodore, among other names. Alternatives of Ted are Ned, Teddy, and Ed.

teddy.a: Teddy is an English language given name, usually a hypocorism of Edward or Theodore or Theodora. It may refer to:

teo.a: Teo is a masculine given name or a nickname for Theodore, Teodor, Teofilo, Mateo, Teoman etc.

teodor.a: Teodor is a masculine given name. In English, it is a cognate of Theodore.

tess.a: Tess is a feminine given name, typically a diminutive form of Theresa or Tessa. It is occasionally a diminutive form of Esther or Hester.

tessa.a: Tessa is a feminine given name, sometimes a shortened form of Theresa. It may refer to:

thady.a: Thady is a male given name—either a diminutive of Thaddeus or derived from the Irish Tadhg—it may refer to: Thady Connellan , Irish school-teacher, poet and historian Thady Coughlan (born 1951), former Limerick City Councillor and former Mayor of Limerick Thady Gosden (born 1995), British racehorse…

thalia.e: From Ancient Greek Θαλία or Θάλεια; from Ancient Greek θάλλω (“flourish, to be verdant”).
thalia.a: Thalia is a feminine given name of ancient Greek origin.

thea.e: Shortened from Dorothea and Theodora, ultimately from Ancient Greek θεά (“goddess”).
thea.a: Thea is a feminine given name, from Greek Θεία, Theía, "Goddess". Other forms include Tea and Téa.

theadora.a: Theodora is a feminine given name, the feminine version of Theodore, from the Greek θεός theos 'god' + δῶρον doron 'gift'. Theodora is first attested in Mycenaean Greek, written in the Linear B syllabic script, as 𐀳𐀃𐀈𐀨, te-o-do-ra. The name Dorothy contains the same word elements in reverse order.

theo.e: Short form of Theodore, or of the rare given names Theobald, Theophilus or Theodoric, or of Theodora.
theo.a: Theo is a given name and a hypocorism.

theodor.a: Theodor is a masculine given name. It is a German form of Theodore. It is also a variant of Teodor.

theodora.e: From Latin Theodora, from Θεοδώρα (“God's Gift”).
theodora.a: Theodora is a feminine given name, the feminine version of Theodore, from the Greek θεός theos 'god' + δῶρον doron 'gift'. Theodora is first attested in Mycenaean Greek, written in the Linear B syllabic script, as 𐀳𐀃𐀈𐀨, te-o-do-ra. The name Dorothy contains the same word elements in reverse order.

theodore.e: The name was popularized in reference to the prominent St Theodore of Amasea. Unrelated to Theodoric.
theodore.a: Theodore is a masculine given name. It comes from the Ancient Greek name Θεόδωρος (Theódoros), meaning "gift of God" . The name was borne by several figures in ancient Greece, such as Theodorus of Samos and Theodorus of Byzantium.

thiago.e: The th in this variant spelling was added unetymologically (see the main entry for the etymology); compare Nathália, a variant spelling of Natália, where a similar unetymological th was added, despite the name coming from nātālis (“natal…

thomas.e: Middle English Thomas, from Latin Thōmās (as in the Vulgate), from Ancient Greek Θωμᾶς, the Biblical Greek transcription of תאומא or תאמא (“twin”), the nickname of one of the Twelve Apostles.
thomas.a: Thomas is a male name of Aramaic origins. The English spelling Thomas is a transliteration through Latin Thomas, of the approximate Greek transliteration , from Imperial Aramaic: תאמא, romanized: Tawmɑʔ), meaning 'twin'.

tia.e: Invented in the latter half of the twentieth century. It can be explained as a short form of Letitia or Venetia, or from Tiia, pet form of Dorothea.
tia.a: Tia is a usually feminine given name with diverse, unrelated origins from multiple cultures. It might have originated as a short form of names containing the word element tia or thea. The word tía is the Portuguese and Spanish word for aunt.

tiana.e: Modern contraction of Tatiana and Christiana. In the USA it is also explained as a form of Diana in such unrelated languages as Samoan and Cherokee (but the author Tiana Bighorse is a Navajo).
tiana.a: Tiana or Tianna is a feminine given name with various origins. It has been used as an extended form of the name Tia or a short form of names such as Cristiana.

tiernan.a: Tiernan is an Irish surname. Tiernan is also an anglicisation of Tiarnán, a given name derived from the Irish word tiarna "lord" + -án (diminutive suffix).

tierney.e: Anglicized from Gaelic Ó Tiarnaigh "descendant of Tiarnach", a diminutive of tiarna (“lord, master”).
tierney.a: Tierney is an Irish surname, and a female given name. The name is an Anglicized form of the Irish language surname Ó Tiarnaigh (literally "Descendant of Tiarnach"; historically spelt Ó Tighearnaigh), derived from tiarna, the Irish word for 'lord' or 'master'. It is sometimes a variant of Tiernan .

tiffany.e: From Old French Tifinie, Tiphanie, from Latin Theophania (“Epiphany”), from Ancient Greek θεο- (“god”) (combining form of θεός (“god”)) + φαίνω (“to shine, appear”).
tiffany.a: Tiffany is a primarily English feminine form of the Greek given name Theophania. It was formerly often given to children born on the feast of Theophania, that is, Epiphany.

tillie.a: Tillie is a feminine given name, a nickname and a surname. It may refer to:

tilly.a: Tilly is a feminine given name or nickname, and a surname. As a female given name or nickname, is generally a variant/diminutive for the Germanic name Matilda. This name may refer to:

timothy.e: From Middle French Timothée, from Latin Tīmotheus, from Ancient Greek Τῑμόθεος, from τῑμάω (“to honour”) + θεός (“god”).
timothy.a: Timothy is a masculine name. It is a version of the Greek name Τιμόθεος meaning 'one who honours God', from τιμή 'honour' and θεός 'god'. Timothy (and its variations) is a common name in several countries.

tobias.e: Ancient Greek Τωβίας, from Hebrew טוֹבִיָּה.

toby.a: Toby is a given name in many English-speaking countries. The name is derived the Middle English vernacular form of Tobias. Tobias itself is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew טוביה Toviah, which translates to Good is Yahweh.

tom.e: From Middle English Thomme. of Thomas. The dollar-bill sense is from the portrait of Thomas Jefferson featured on it.
tom.a: Tom is a masculine given name, often used as a diminutive of Thomas. In Germanic countries and Scandinavia, "Tom" is in use as a formal given name. The Gaelic-Cymric name Tom means "rising ground" or "eminent".

tomas.a: Tomás is a Spanish, Portuguese, and Irish (also in the archaic forms Thomaz, Thomás and Tomaz) given name equivalent of Thomas.

tomi.a: Tomi is a common name. In Finnish, it is a variant of Thomas and primarily used as a masculine name. In Japan, it can be a feminine or masculine given name.

tommie.a: Tommie is a masculine given name of English origin, occasionally a nickname or shortened form of Thomas, and is sometimes used as a feminine form of Thomas. Notable people with the name include:

tommy.a: Tommy is a masculine given name, frequently a short form of Thomas. An alternative spelling is Thommy. It may refer to:

tony.a: Tony is an English masculine given name that occurs as a diminutive form of Anthony or Antonio in many countries. As a diminutive form of Antonia or Antonietta, it is found in Denmark, Finland, Greenland, Norway, and Sweden.

torin.a: Torin is a masculine given name which may refer to: People: Torin Dorn (born 1968), American former National Football League player Torin Ferguson (born 1985), football goalkeeper from the Bahamas Torin Francis (born 1983), American professional basketball player Torin Koos (born 1980), American…

travis.e: From an word meaning "to cross over," related to traverse. Probably a name for a gatekeeper or the toll collector of a bridge.
travis.a: Travis is mainly an English masculine given name of French origin. It is derived from the word "traverser" or "to cross", and was given to toll collectors who stood by a bridge or crossing.

tristan.a: Tristan, Tristram, or Tristen is a given name derived from Welsh drust (meaning "noise", "tumult"), influenced by the French word triste and Welsh/Cornish/Breton trist, both of which mean "bold" or "sad", "sorrowful".

troy.e: From Latin Troia, from Ancient Greek Τροία.
troy.a: Troy is a male given first name used in English-speaking countries, and may derive from the Irish Troightheach, meaning "foot soldier". Additionally Troy is utilised as an anglicised surname derived from a variety of Gaelic and Norman surnames. Further detail here Troy (surname).

tudor.a: Tudor is a surname and given name of Welsh origin, and also a separate name of Romanian origin. The Welsh name comes from the Brythonic Tudur, itself a derivation of Toutorīx which was conflated with Tewdwr or Tewdr. It is related to the name Theodore.

tully.a: Tully is a unisex, given name derived from the surname.

tyler.e: From Middle English Tyler, Tylere, Tygler, Tygheler, Tyghelere, Tyghelare, Tygelere, from Middle English tiler, tylere, tylare, tylier (“tiler”).
tyler.a: Tyler is a given name that is gender-neutral but predominantly male, as well as a surname. It is an Old English name derived from the Old French tieuleor, tieulier (tiler, tile maker) and the Middle English tyler, tylere.

tymon.a: Tymon is a surname and male given name. Notable people with this name include:

tyrone.a: Tyrone is a male given name of Irish origin. The name originates from the toponym County Tyrone in Northern Ireland, which in turn derives from the Irish language Tír Eoghain ("land of Eoghan"). Tír Eoghain was the name of a Gaelic kingdom of medieval Ireland.

tyson.a: Tyson is an English male given name of old French origin meaning 'high-spirited', 'fire'. It is from this that a surname arose 'son of Tyson'.

ultan.a: Ultan is an Irish male given name derived from Ulster.

umar.e: From Arabic عُمَر. See also Umari.
umar.a: Umar is a masculine given name.

una.a: Una is a feminine given name with various origins. As used by Edmund Spenser in The Faerie Queene, the name is derived from the Latin unus, meaning one.

usman.e: Via an intermediary language, such as عُثْمَان, or Usman, from Arabic عُثْمَان.
usman.a: Osman refers to two different names: Osman or Usman is the Turkish, Kurdish, Persian, and Urdu transliteration of the Arabic masculine given name Uthman.

uzair.a: Uzair , also spelled "Uzayr" or "Ozair", is a male name. It is the Arabic equivalent of the Hebrew name "Ezra", and it means "helper" or "strength". The name originated from the Islamic prophet "Uzair", who is often identified as the biblical prophet "Ezra".

valencia.e: From Spanish Valencia, from Latin Valentia, from valentia (“power, vigour”).

valentina.e: From, and Latin Valentīna, feminine forms of and Italian Valentino, and Latin Valentīnus.
valentina.a: Valentina is a feminine given name. It is a feminine form of the Roman name Valentinus, which is derived from the Latin word "valens" meaning "healthy, strong".

valentino.a: Valentino is an Italian male given name, the masculine equivalent of the female given name Valentina. It may be abbreviated as "Vale" or "Tino". The equivalent English male given name is Valentine.

valerie.e: From French Valérie, from Latin Valeria.
valerie.a: Valerie is generally a feminine given name, derived directly from the French Valérie (a traditionally female name). Valéry or Valery is a masculine given name in parts of Europe (particularly in France and Russia), as well as a common surname in Francophone countries.

vanessa.a: Vanessa is a feminine given name. It was created by the Anglo-Irish writer Jonathan Swift for Esther Vanhomrigh, whom Swift had met in 1708 and whom he tutored. The name was created by taking "Van" from Vanhomrigh's last name and adding "Essa", a pet form of Esther.

vera.e: Borrowed in the nineteenth century from the virtue name Ве́ра (“faith”). By folk etymology it has also been explained as Latin vera (“true”).
vera.a: Vera is a female given name of Slavic origin, the translation of old Christian name with Latin form Fides (Faith, Foy) and Greek Πίστις (Pistis). The name Vera has been used in the English speaking world since the 19th century and was popular in the early 20th century.

verity.a: Verity (alias Veretie, Verety, Verita, Veritie, etc.) is a female first name and a surname. As a first name it derives from the Latin feminine noun veritas, meaning "truth".

veronica.e: From the form of Berenice, from Ancient Greek Φερενίκη. Influenced by the Church Latin phrase vera icon ("true image") associated with the veil of Saint Veronica, who wiped the face of Jesus on the way to Calvary, resulting in an image of…
veronica.a: Veronica is a female given name, a Latin alteration of the ancient Macedonian name Berenice , which in turn is derived from the Macedonian form of the Attic Greek Φερενίκη, Phereníkē, or Φερονίκη, Pheroníkē, from φέρειν, phérein, to bring, and νίκη, níkê, "victory", i.e. "she who brings victory".

victor.e: From a personal name Victor, borne by several saints, from victor (“conqueror”).
victor.a: Victor or Viktor is a given name and a surname. It is Latin in origin, meaning winner or conqueror, and the word “victor” still means this in Modern English. Victor is an early Christian name, borne by several saints and three popes, symbolizing Jesus' victory over both sin and death.

victoria.e: From Latin Victōria, from victōria (“victory”). The given name can also be analyzed as the male name Victor + ia. The places were named in honour of Queen Victoria of Great Britain.
victoria.a: Victoria is a feminine given name.

vienna.e: From and Vienna, from German Wien, Middle High German Wienne, and Old High German Wienna, probably from Proto-Celtic *widus (“wood”) or *weidus (“wild”) via unattested *Vedunia.

viktor.a: Victor or Viktor is a given name and a surname. It is Latin in origin, meaning winner or conqueror, and the word “victor” still means this in Modern English. Victor is an early Christian name, borne by several saints and three popes, symbolizing Jesus' victory over both sin and death.

vincent.e: French Vincent, from Latin Vincentius, from vincēns (“conquering”), from the verb vincō.
vincent.a: Vincent (Latin: Vincentius) is a masculine given name originating from the Roman name Vincentius, which itself comes from the Latin verb vincere, meaning "to conquer."

vincenzo.a: Vincenzo is an Italian male given name, derived from the Latin name Vincentius (the verb vincere means to win or to conquer). Notable people with the name include:

vinnie.a: Vinny or Vinnie is a masculine given name, usually a shortened version of Vincent, Vincenzo, Arvin, or Vicente, which may refer to:

vinny.a: Vinny or Vinnie is a masculine given name, usually a shortened version of Vincent, Vincenzo, Arvin, or Vicente, which may refer to:

violet.e: A 19th century flower name from violet, sometimes as an anglicisation of the earlier French Violette.
violet.a: Violet is a female given name which comes from the eponymous flower. As with other such names, its popularity has varied dramatically over time.

vivienne.a: Vivian (and variants such as Vivien and Vivienne) is a given name, and less often a surname, derived from a Latin name of the Roman Empire period, masculine Vivianus and feminine Viviana, which survived into modern use because it is the name of two early Christian female martyrs as well as of a…

vlad.e: Common male given name, sometimes used as a short form of Vladimir, but more commonly a hypocorism of Vladislav. It is also found as and surname.
vlad.a: Vlad is a Romanian male name. It is more commonly a nativized hypocorism of Vladislav and can also be used as a surname. Alternately, it may be a hypocoristic form of the Slavic name Vladimir (although the normative nickname is Vova).

vladimir.e: From Russian Владимир, as well as from other Slavic cognates, and reinforced by Vladimirus, name of several saints in the Eastern Orthodox Church, from Володимѣръ, Владимѣръ, from *Voldiměrъ (which see for more), equivalent to владь…
vladimir.a: Vladimir is a masculine given name of Slavic origin, widespread throughout all Slavic nations in different forms and spellings.

walter.e: A name, from Middle English Walter, from Waltier, from *Waltheri (compare Old High German Waltheri, which see for more details), from Proto-West Germanic *Waldahari, from Proto-Germanic *Waldaharjaz, from *waldą + *harjaz.
walter.a: Walter is a German and English masculine given name of Germanic origin, composed of the elements meaning "power" or "ruler", and "army".

wesley.e: Several places in England, from Old English west (“west”) + lēah (“wood, clearing”). Equivalent to west + -leigh.

wiktor.a: Wiktor is a Polish masculine given name. It is the Polish form of the name Victor, meaning "winner" or "conqueror". The feminine form of the name is Wiktoria.

wilbur.e: From an female given name Wilburg, from wil (“will”) + burh (“fortress”).
wilbur.a: Wilbur is an English and German masculine given name of Germanic origin as well as a surname. The etymology of the name is disputed, however the most accepted theory is that it is composed of the Germanic elements wilþī- (Proto-Germanic *wilþijaz-) "wild", and ebur (Proto-Germanic *eburaz) "boar".

wilf.a: Wilf is a masculine given name, most commonly a diminutive form of Wilfred or Wilfrid. It is also a nickname and a surname.

wilfred.e: The name of two early Anglo-Saxon saints Wilfriþ, from wil + friþ.
wilfred.a: Wilfred is a masculine given name derived from Germanic roots meaning "will" and "peace" . The name was popular in the United Kingdom in the early twentieth century. Wilfried and its English spelling, Wilfrid, are closely related to Wilfred, with the same roots (Will and Frieden in German).

willa.e: Derived from Wilhelmina and recoined in the 19th century in America based on the male given names Will and William.
willa.a: Willa is a feminine given name.

william.e: From Middle English William, from Anglo-Norman Willame, from Old High German Willahelm, from Proto-Germanic *Wiljahelmaz (> Latin Gulielmus), from Proto-Germanic *wiljô (“will”) + *helmaz (“helmet”), ultimately from the roots *welh₁- (“to…
william.a: William is a masculine given name of Germanic origin. It became popular in England after the Norman conquest in 1066, and remained so throughout the Middle Ages and into the modern era.

willow.a: Willow is a given name used in reference to the willow. It has grown in popularity in English speaking countries along with other names inspired by the natural world.

winifred.e: From Old English Winfriþ, from Welsh Gwenfrewi.

winnie.a: Winnie or Winny ( WIN-ee) is both a male and a female given name of Welsh origin, a short form (hypocorism) of Edwina, Winona, Winifred or Winnifred, Winter, Gwendolyn, Guinevere (Welsh), Gwyneth (Welsh), and Wynne (Welsh).

winston.e: From personal name Wine, in the genitive singular case Wines + tūn (“farm, village”).

winter.a: Winter is a unisex given name of English origin given in reference to the season. In some instances, the given name is a transferred use of the surname. The name has been in regular use across the English-speaking world.

woody.a: Woody, also spelled Woodie, is a masculine given name in its own right or a pet form of Woodrow and other names such as Elwood or Heywood. It was especially popular in the US during and after the presidency of Woodrow Wilson. It is also a surname.

wren.e: Originally a nickname, from Middle English wrenne (“wren”).
wren.a: Wren is both an English surname and a gender neutral given name, both derived from the English name of the songbird. It has recently increased in popularity as a name for girls and boys in the Anglosphere along with other names derived from the natural world.

wyatt.e: Ultimately from the personal name Wigheard, from wīg (“war”) + heard (“hard, brave”), later also used as a diminutive of the names Guy and William.
wyatt.a: Wyatt is a male given name, derived from the Norman surname Guyot, derived from "widu", Proto-Germanic for "wood".

xanthe.e: From Ancient Greek Ξανθή, from ξανθός (“yellow”).
xanthe.a: Xanthe is a name with origins in Greek mythology.

xavier.e: From Medieval Latin Xavierus and Spanish Xavier, variant of Javier, ultimately from Xabier. Originally chiefly in honor of the Navarrese saint Francis Xavier. Doublet of Echeverría.
xavier.a: The given name Xavier is a masculine name derived from the 16th-century Navarrese Roman Catholic Saint Francis Xavier.

yahya.e: From Arabic يَحْيَى, equivalent to John in the Qur'an.
yahya.a: Yahya, Yahyo, or Yahiya is a masculine given name and surname of Arabic origin. In the Qur'an, Yahya also appears as the Arabic equivalent of the given name of the prophet John the Baptist in Islam. For this reason, Yahya is now a common name in the Muslim world.

yanis.a: Yannis, Yanis, Yiannis, or Giannis is a common Greek given name, a variant of John meaning "God is gracious." In formal Greek (e.g. all government documents and birth certificates) the name exists only as Ioannis .

yara.a: Yara (or Iara) is a given name developed independently in the Arabic and Tupi languages, and also the anglicized spelling of a number of unrelated given names.

yaseen.a: Yaseen is an Arabic-based name and a variant of Yasin, Yassin, Yassine and Yacine. It is an Arabic-based unisex name used frequently in the Arab World and Muslim countries, and a surname. The name comes from a chapter (surah) of the Quran called Ya-Sin.

yasin.a: Yasin is a surname and unisex given name of Arabic origin. The name comes from a chapter (surah) of the Quran called Ya-Sin. Variants include Yassin, Yassine, Yaseen, and Yacine.

yasir.a: Yasser is an Arabic male name meaning "to be of ease" or "of wealth".

yasmin.e: Variant of Jasmine, often representing a transliteration of the corresponding and names.
yasmin.a: Yasmin is a feminine given name of Persian origin , sometimes also used as a surname. Notable people with the name include:

yasmine.e: Variant of Jasmine, often representing a transliteration of the corresponding and names.

younes.a: Yunus , also spelled Younas, Younes, Younis, Younous, Younus, Yunes, Yunis, Yunos and Yonas, is a common male given name, the Arabic version of the Greek Ιωνάς (Ionas), from the Hebrew יוֹנָה Jonah 'dove'.

yousef.e: Arabic يُوسُف, equivalent to English Joseph.
yousef.a: Yusuf is an Arabic male name meaning "increases" (in piety, power and influence). It is the Arabic equivalent of the Hebrew name Yosef and the English name Joseph.

yousuf.a: Yusuf is an Arabic male name meaning "increases" (in piety, power and influence). It is the Arabic equivalent of the Hebrew name Yosef and the English name Joseph.

yumna.a: Yumna is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. Notable people with this name include:

yunus.e: Arabic يُونُس, from Ancient Greek Ἰωνᾶς, from Hebrew יונה.
yunus.a: Yunus , also spelled Younas, Younes, Younis, Younous, Younus, Yunes, Yunis, Yunos and Yonas, is a common male given name, the Arabic version of the Greek Ιωνάς (Ionas), from the Hebrew יוֹנָה Jonah 'dove'.

yusha.a: Yusha or Yushān is a masculine given name, the Arabic form of Joshua which is of Hebrew origin, meaning "God is salvation".

yusra.a: Yousra, Yosra, or Yusra is a feminine given name of Arabic origin. It is the feminine equivalent of Yousri. Notable people with the name include:

yusuf.e: Arabic يُوسُف, from Biblical Hebrew יוֹסֵף.
yusuf.a: Yusuf is an Arabic male name meaning "increases" (in piety, power and influence). It is the Arabic equivalent of the Hebrew name Yosef and the English name Joseph.

zac.a: Zac is a masculine given name, often a short form (hypocorism) of Zachary. It may refer to:

zach.a: Zach is the given name or nickname of: Zach Aguilar (born 1998), American voice actor Zach Allen (born 1997), American football player Zach Bako-Bewele (born 1999), American football player Zach Banner (born 1993), American football player Zach Boren (born 1991), American football player Zach…

zachariah.e: From Hebrew זְכַרְיָה (“Yahweh has remembered”) under influence from Latin Zacharias and Ζαχαρίας.

zachary.e: From clipped forms of Zachariah and Zacharias + -y, from Hebrew זְכַרְיָה (“Yahweh has remembered”) via Latin Zacharias and Ζαχαρίας.
zachary.a: Zachary is a male given name, a variant of Zechariah – the name of several biblical characters.

zack.a: Zack (and variant spellings Zach, Zac, Zak, Zakk) is sometimes a given name, but more often it is a hypocorism or short form of another given name, usually Zachary in the English speaking world, which derives from Zechariah.

zackary.a: Zackary is a given name. It is alternate spelling of Zachary.

zahra.e: Borrowed from Arabic زَهْراء, an epithet of Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad. As a surname, it is predominantly found in Egypt.
zahra.a: Zahra is a female given name and surname. It became popular as the name of Muhammad’s daughter, Fatimah al-Zahra. The name was also popularized by Muslim influence in the Indian subcontinent.

zaid.a: Zaid or Zayd is an Arabic given name and surname.

zaina.a: Zaina is a given name. Notable people with the given name include: Zaina Agoro, Nigerian American singer-songwriter Zaina Erhaim, Syrian journalist and feminist Zaina Hassan (born 2004), Jordanian footballer Zaina Kapepula (born 1975), Congolese basketball player

zainab.a: Zaynab , and variant spellings, is an Arabic female given name meaning 'a flower in the desert'. Zainab bint Muhammad was a daughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, Zaynab bint Ali was a granddaughter, two of his wives were Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zaynab bint Khuzayma.

zak.a: Zak (or Zakk) is a given name derived from Zachary or Zechariah/Zachariah.

zakariya.e: From Arabic زَكَرِيَّا, from ܙܟ݂ܼܿܪܝܵܐ, from Hebrew זְכַרְיָה (“Yahweh has remembered”).
zakariya.a: Zakariya is a masculine given name, the Arabic form of Zechariah which is of Hebrew origin, meaning "God/Yahweh has remembered".

zane.a: Zane is a unisex given name and a surname. Its Western usage derives from the Venetian form of Gianni or an alternate spelling of the German and Jewish name Zahn. Zane can also refer to the Arabic personal name more commonly spelt Zain meaning "beautiful" or "handsome".

zara.e: A 20th-century variant of Sarah, or explained as Arabic زَهْرَة (“flower”); given to the daughter of Princess Anne in 1981.
zara.a: Zara is a feminine given name and a surname. Zara is commonly cited as a Hebrew name and considered a variant of the Hebrew name Sarah or a feminine form of Zarah, better known as Zerah, a biblical figure from the Book of Genesis.

zayd.a: Zaid or Zayd is an Arabic given name and surname.

zayden.e: American 21st-century coinage, rhyming with Jayden, Brayden, Aidan, etc.
zayden.a: Zayden () is a variant of the male given name Aidan (name). The popularity of Zayden as a baby name in the United States peaked in 2014 when it reached 188th. The name entered into usage over the late 1990s and early 2000s decade.

zaynab.a: Zaynab , and variant spellings, is an Arabic female given name meaning 'a flower in the desert'. Zainab bint Muhammad was a daughter of the Islamic prophet Muhammad, Zaynab bint Ali was a granddaughter, two of his wives were Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zaynab bint Khuzayma.

zayne.a: Zayne and Zayn are alternative ways of writing the given name Zane, as well as romanizations of the Arabic unisex given name Zain , meaning "Beauty". Zayn and Zayne may refer to:

zeke.a: Zeke is a masculine given name and nickname, and is sometimes a shortened form (hypocorism) of Ezekiel, which may refer to:

zeynep.a: Zeynep is the Turkish form of the Arabic female given name Zaynab. Zeynep means "precious rock, precious gem" and may refer to:

zidan.a: Zidan or more formally Zaydan is a given name and family name in various cultures. As an Arabic name it is also romanised as Zidane or Zeidan. As a Chinese given name, it can be written in various ways , with different meanings depending on the component Chinese characters.

ziggy.a: Ziggy is a masculine given name, often a diminutive form (hypocorism) of Zigmunt and other names. It is also a nickname. Notable people with the name include:

zion.e: From Middle English Sion, from Old English Syon, from Sīōn, from Σῑών, from Biblical Hebrew צִיּוֹן. Initial Z- was likely under influence from Zion, itself influenced by the Ashkenazi pronunciation.
zion.a: Zion is a given name and surname derived from the ancient Canaanite hill fortress in Jerusalem called the City of David. It is less commonly spelled Sion, Tzion, Tsion, Tsiyon, Seyon, or Tsiyyon. In Hebrew Zion is one of the 70 Names of Jerusalem.

zoe.a: Zoe is a feminine first name of Greek origin, meaning "life."

zoey.a: Zoe is a feminine first name of Greek origin, meaning "life."

zofia.a: Zofia is a Slavic given name of Old Greek origin, meaning wisdom. It is a variant of Sofia.

zuri.a: Zuri is a given name of Swahili origin meaning "beautiful." It has been among the 1,000 most popular names for newborn girls in the United States since 2010 and among the top 300 names since 2018.

zuzanna.e: First recorded as a given name of Latvians in 1608. Ultimately. Cognate to English Susan.
zuzanna.a: Zuzana is a common female given name in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. It is often translated to other languages as Zuzanna (Polish), Zsuzsanna (Hungarian), Suzanne, Susan, or Susannah – all commonly derived from the Hebrew language name Shoshana, meaning "lily".
